LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3235 
TO BE ANSWERED ON FRIDAY, THE 07th AUGUST, 2026 
 
PROGRESS ON LEGISLATIVE REFORMS 
3235. SHRI BALRAM NAIK PORIKA: 
Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be pleased to state: 
(a) the progress made in legislative reforms, the new laws enacted to promote ease of doing 
business and their implementation status; 
(b) the details of alternate dispute resolution mechanisms (mediation and arbitration) promoted 
and the number of cases resolved; 
(c) the impact on contract enforcement and India’s ranking in World Bank Ease of Doing 
Business parameters; and 
(d) whether any performance audit has been conducted on judicial infrastructure development 
and the timely delivery of justice, if so, the details thereof?” 
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF 
 LAW AND JUSTICE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
 
(SHRI ARJUN RAM MEGHWAL) 
(a): Legislative and policy interventions along with related reforms for promoting ease of doing 
business is a continuous process being undertaken by the Government, keeping in view the 
changing requirements of the stakeholders.  The Government continues to take steps to reduce 
the criminalisation of minor violations and replace them with more proportionate civil penalties 
and administrative mechanisms under various enactments. In this regard, recognising the need 
to make laws more balanced and practical, t he Government began a process of reviewing 
provisions. An important step in this direction was the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) 
Act, 2023, which removed criminal penalties for a number of minor offences across several 
Central laws. Pursuant theret o, the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2026 was 
published in the Official Gazette on 8 April 2026, which rationalizes provisions across 79 

2 
 
Central Acts administered by 23 Ministries and Departments. The reforms are aimed at 
promoting trust -based governance, reducing compliance burden, improving ease of doing 
business, and ensuring proportionate regulatory enforcement. 
(b): The Government continues to promote alternate dispute resolution (ADR) mechanisms 
including arbitration and mediation in the country, as these mechanisms are less adversarial 
and are capable of providing a better substitute to the conventional methods of r esolving 
disputes. The Government is further taking policy and legislative interventions, to strengthen 
these mechanisms and make them more efficacious and expeditious.  
The major initiatives, steps and measures taken by the Central Government over the years in 
this regard include with respect to the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 which has been 
progressively amended in the years 2015, 2019 and 2020 to keep pace wi th current 
developments in the arbitration landscape and to enable arbitration as a viable dispute 
resolution mechanism. The amendments are aimed at ensuring timely conclusion of 
arbitration proceedings, neutrality of arbitrators, minimizing judicial intervention in the arbitral 
process, efficacious enforcement of arbitral awards and promotion of institutional arbitration. 
The Commercial Courts Act, 2015 was also amended in the year 2018 to provide inter-alia for 
Pre-Institution Mediation and Settlement (PIMS) mechanism. Under this mechanism, where a 
commercial dispute of specified value does not contemplate any urgent interim relief, the 
parties have to first exhaust the mandatory remedy of PIMS before approaching the Court. This 
is aimed at providing an opportunity to the parties to resolve the commercial disputes through 
mediation.  
The India International Arbitration Centre Act, 2019, was enacted to provide for the 
establishment of the India International Arbitration Centre for the purpose of creating an 
independent, autonomous and world class body for facilitating institutional arbi tration and to 
declare the Centre to be an institution of national importance. The Centre has since been 
established and aims to inspire confidence amongst parties, both domestic and international, 
by providing a neutral dispute resolution platform for res olution of commercial disputes 
through arbitration.  
The Mediation Act, 2023, lays down the legislative framework for mediation to be adopted by 
disputing parties, especially under the aegis of institutional mediation. The Mediation Act, 2023 
is also expected to be a pivotal legislative intervention towards providing standalone law on 
mediation and enabling the growth of a culture of amicable settlement of disputes out of court. 
Further, the aforesaid interventions from time to time have contributed towards improving and 
strengthening the ADR landscape, supporting the ease of doing business and enabling the 
country being seen as an attractive destination for investments and economic growth.

(c) & (d): The Law Commission, in its 120th Report  (1987), has recommended a judge -to-
population ratio of 50 judges per million of the Indian population.  Further, in 245th Report 
(2014), the Law Commission observed that filing of cases per capita varies substantially 
across geographical units as filings are associated with economic and social conditions of the 
population. As such the Law Commission did not consider the judge population ratio to be a 
scientific criterion for determining the adequacy of the judge strength in the country. The Law 
Commission found the “Rate of Disposal” method appropriate, which aims at the number of 
additional judges required to clear the backlog of cases and ensuring that new backlog is not 
created to be more pragmatic and useful. 
 
In August 2014, the Supreme Court asked the National Court Management System 
Committee (NCMS Committee) to examine the recommendations made by the Law 
Commission and to furnish its recommendations in this regard. NCMS Committee submitted 
its report to the Supreme Court in March, 2016. The Committee has proposed a “ weighted” 
disposal approach i.e. disposal weighted by the nature and complexity of cases in local 
conditions. As per the direction of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in its Order dated 02.01.2017, 
the Department of Justice has forwarded a copy of interim report of the NCMS Committee to 
all the State Governments and High Courts to enable them to take follow up action to 
determine the required strength of district and subordinate judiciary.

3242.   Shri Manickam Tagore B: 
            
   Will the Minister of Chemicals and Fertilizers be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether it is a fact that farmers are being forced to purchase alternative 
additional fertilizers due to shortage of DAP, if so, the details thereof along with the 
steps taken to ensure adequate availability of DAP during agricultural cropping 
seasons; 
 
(b) the details of fertilizer subsidy allocated, released and utilized for Urea and 
DAP during the last three years and the current financial year, along with its impact 
on retail prices for farmers, year-wise; 
 
(c) whether the Government proposes to increase domestic production capacity 
of Urea and DAP to reduce dependence on imports and ensure fertilizer security, if 
so, the details thereof; 
 
(d) whether any assessment has been conducted by the Government regarding 
the impact of Urea and DAP availability and prices on the cost of cultivation and 
farmers’ income, if so, the findings thereof; and 
 
(e) whether the Government has taken steps to improve fertilizer distribution 
through digital monitoring systems such as real-time tracking of stocks, movement 
and sales of Urea and DAP, if so, the details thereof? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS 
 
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
 
(a) to (e) Following steps are taken by the Government every season for ensuring 
timely and adequate availability of DAP and other fertilizers in the country: 
 
(i) Before the commencement of each cropping season, Department of Agriculture 
and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with all the State Governments, 
assesses the State-wise & month-wise requirement of fertilizers. On the basis of 
requirement projected by DA&FW, Department of Fertilizers (DoF) allocates 
adequate quantities of fertilizers to States by issuing monthly supply plan and 
continuously monitors the availability. 
 

(ii) The movement of all major subsidized fertilizers is monitored throughout the country 
by an on-line web-based monitoring system called integrated Fertilizer Management 
System (iFMS). 
 
(iii) The gap between demand (requirement) and production for Urea & other fertilizers 
is met through imports. The import for the season is also finalized well in advance 
to ensure timely availability.  
 
(iv) The State Governments are regularly advised to coordinate with manufacturers and 
importers for streamlining the supplies through timely placement of indents. 
 
(v) Regular coordination is done with the Ministry of Railways for giving sufficient rakes, 
priority to fertilizers and for timely evacuation of rakes for States. 
 
(vi) The distribution of fertilizers within the State at district/block level is done by the 
concerned State government. 
 
In view of above, the availability of DAP in the country has remained adequate during the 
ongoing Kharif 2026 season. The State-wise information regarding requirement, availability, 
sales and closing stock of DAP for the period  01.04.2026 to 03.08.2026 is placed at 
Annexure A. 
 
The details of total fertilizer subsidy allocated, disbursed during the last three years 
i.e. 2023-24 to 2025-26 and current financial year 2026-27 (as on 04.08.2026) by the 
Government is placed at Annexure B.

statutorily notified Maximum Retail Price (MRP). The MRP of 45 kg bag of urea is Rs.242 
per bag (exclusive of charges towards neem coating and taxes as applicable). The 
difference between the delivered cost of urea at farm gate and net market realization by the 
urea units is given as subsidy to the urea manufacturer/importer by the Government of India. 
Accordingly, all farmers are being supplied urea at the subsidized rate.

Poshan Tracker to evaluate its impact on delivery of nutrition and child development 
services under Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0, if so, the details thereof;  
(b)  whether such assessment has identified any challenges relating to digital authentication, 
data quality/service delivery through Poshan Tracker, if so, the details thereof;  
(c)  whether the Government has prescribed any mechanism for periodic evaluation of the 
impact of the Poshan Tracker on beneficiary coverage and service delivery, if so, the 
details thereof; and 
(d)  the details of the measures taken/proposed to be taken to address the challenges 
identified and strengthen the implementation of the POSHAN Tracker?  
  
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR)  
  
(a) to (d): To review the progress of the Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 digitally, 
the Ministry of Women and Child Development (MoWCD ) has introduced ‘Poshan Tracker’ 
application as an ICT based governance tool. It provides facility for monitoring and review of 
all services provided to the beneficiaries at Anganwadi Centres and also at their home. Poshan 
Tracker has enabled the Ministry , as well as States and UTs to continuously review the 
implementation of the Mission on various parameters and to make course correction.  
An outcome -based evaluation study of Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 was 
conducted by Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office  (DMEO), NITI Aayog (2025). 
As per the study, digitalization through Poshan Tracker Application has a multi -dimensional 
impact on nutrition monitoring, Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE), beneficiary 
authentication, and service delivery efficiency. The Report highlighted Poshan Tracker as a 
significant shift from manual, paper -based systems to a technology -enabled governance 

framework under the Supplementary Nutrition Programme (SNP). As per the report, Poshan 
Tracker has become the cornerstone for digital monitoring of beneficiaries, inventory, and 
service delivery at Anganwadi Centres (AWCs). The expansion of digital platfor ms like the 
Poshan Tracker represents a foundational shift in governance, enabling greater responsiveness, 
efficiency, and transparency in the SNP’s last-mile delivery. Further, in pursuance to the Union 
Budget Speech of 2016, every scheme has been aligned  with the Finance Commission cycles 
and its continuation is based on the evaluation of scheme by a third party.  
To address network -related issues while using Poshan Tracker, such as low or no internet 
connectivity in some areas, the application provides offline functionality for conducting e-KYC 
and face matching under the Facial Recognition System (FRS) for distrib ution of Take-Home 
Ration (THR). OTP for e-KYC and Aadhar face matching has to be taken ONCE in the entire 
life cycle of a beneficiary. It creates ease of living for the beneficiaries to avail the Anganwadi 
services even when network or server issues are present. The data entered on the application in 
the offline mode has provision of 5 days to sync, once network restores.

effective use of the Poshan Tracker application through the following mechanisms:  
• Learning Videos and awareness documents: In the Resource section of the Poshan 
Tracker application, learning videos and awareness documents are available for 
Anganwadi Workers which can be accessed by them at any point of time for effective 
delivery of their routine tasks. 
• Under the Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi (PBPB) initiative, the MoWCD  is imparting training 
to all the officials and field functionaries in the States and UTs through a cascading 
model of training, wherein Master Trainers (District Officers, Block Coordinators and 
Supervisors) are trained, and the master trainers further tr ain all Anganwadi Workers 
in the field. Training is imparted on different modules of Poshan Tracker, viz. Facial 
Recognition System (FRS), Geo -Tagging, Home Visit Scheduler etc. Block and 
District coordinators provide on -ground handholding support to AWWs and 
supervisors for effective usage of the Poshan Tracker Application and resolution of 
technical glitches. 
• Daily Virtual Classroom Sessions: Digital India Corporation (DIC) organises virtual

Anganwadi Workers may join to raise operational queries and receive real -time 
clarifications on use of the application. Further, traini

ARCTIC POLICY OF INDIA
3244. SHRI RAO RAJENDRA SINGH
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state:-
(a) the measures taken by the Government under Arctic Policy of India to 
strengthen transportation and connectivity with the Nordic countries;
(b) the steps taken in coordination with the Nordic countries to mitigate  
climate change under India's Arctic Policy; and
(c) the manner in which India's partnership with the Nordic countries is  
strengthening maritime and environmental cooperation?

2
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH)
(a) to (c) India’s Arctic Policy, titled “India and the Arctic: Building a  
Partnership for Sustainable Development”, was released in 2022. Guided  
by  the  Policy,  India  works  closely  with  all  the  Nordic  countries  on 
connectivity, climate action and maritime and environmental cooperation, 
including through Summit-level engagement.
At the 3 rd India-Nordic Summit, held in Norway on 19 May 2026, it  
was  decided  to  elevate  the  India-Nordic  relationship  to  a  Green 
Technology and Innovation Strategic Partnership. The leaders also agreed 
to improve connectivity between the Nordic and the Indo-Pacific regions, 
in line with the continued development of the India-Middle East-Europe  
Economic Corridor. There is also direct air connectivity with Finland and  
Denmark.
On climate change, India and the Nordic countries are working  
together on renewable energy, green hydrogen, zero- and low-emission  
technologies such as carbon capture, utilisation and storage and critical  
minerals in support of  the transition to clean energy and sustainable  
economic growth. The Leadership Group for Industry Transition (LeadIT),  

3
launched by India and Sweden in 2019 to reduce emissions from industry, 
has since been joined by most Nordic countries.
Maritime  and  environmental  cooperation  is  being  strengthened 
through  bilateral  dialogues  and  the  Indo-Pacific  Oceans  Initiative, 
covering maritime safety, welfare of seafarers, prevention of pollution at  
sea,  green  shipping,  shipbuilding,  sustainable  ship  recycling  and  
sustainable  management  of  ocean  resources.  India  has  recently  
commenced Maritime Security Dialogues with Nordic countries, including 
Norway and Denmark.
India also continues its scientific work in the Arctic through its  
research station, Himadri, in Svalbard, where winter expeditions have  
been undertaken since December 2023. India’s National Centre for Polar  
and Ocean Research collaborates with institutions in the Nordic countries 
to study changes in Arctic glaciers, ocean life and marine pollution.

entries.head:

CASES OF NIPAH VIRUS IN WEST BENGAL
3245. SHRI ASADUDDIN OWAISI:
Will the MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:-
(a) whether the Government is aware of the recent cases of Nipah virus outbreak reported in
West Bengal, with at least five confirmed cases and the existing of the virus in Kerala, if so,
the details thereof;
(b) the specific measures being taken by the Government to prevent the zoonotic transmission
from animals to humans, including the details of active surveillance in the affected regions;
(c) whether the Government has issued any advisory for the commencement of screening for
Nipah in containment zones across the country along with the details of critical care support
in this regard;
(d) the measures taken by the Government to contain the outbreak, given its high fatality rate
of 40 per cent to 75 per cent and the absence of approved vaccines or antivirals;
(e) whether a public health advisory has been issued to raise awareness about symptoms,
prevention and hygiene in the country, if so, the details thereof; and
(f) whether the Government is aware that Thailand and Singapore are screening passengers
arriving from West Bengal, if so, the details of the specific travel advisories issued for
outbound passengers from the affected regions?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY
WELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) to (e): The Government is aware of the reported cases of Nipah virus disease in the States
of West Bengal and Kerala. During 2026, West Bengal reported two laboratory-confirmed
cases of Nipah virus disease, including one death, while Kerala reported one laboratory-
confirmed case. All reported cases were promptly investigated by the respective State
Governments with technical support from the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC).
National Joint Outbreak Response Teams (NJORTs) were deployed to both West Bengal and
Kerala to support epidemiological investigations, strengthen surveillance, facilitate contact
tracing, and assist the States in implementing appropriate public health measures for
containment of the outbreaks.
The details of the measures undertaken by the Government to prevent the zoonotic
transmission from animals to humans and to contain the outbreak are at Annexure.

The NCDC has developed and disseminated technical guidance documents, including
standard operating procedures, Learning Resource Packages and Communicable Disease
Alert to support uniform preparedness, surveillance, diagnosis and response across States and
Union Territories. The details may be seen on the links:
(https://ncdc.mohfw.gov.in/uploads/resource/1769335263_ZDPHI_Manual_2025_V2_06.11.
2025.pdf) and (https://ncdc.mohfw.gov.in/uploads/glimpse_pdfs/1770282425_CD-Alert-
NIPAH-Virus.pdf)
To strengthen risk communication and community awareness, NCDC has developed and
disseminated a range of Information, Education and Communication (IEC) materials,
including print, audio and video resources, on priority zoonotic diseases, including Nipah
Virus Disease. These materials are used for training of healthcare professionals as well as for
public awareness and community outreach activities. The details may be accessed at link:
https://ncdc.mohfw.gov.in/includes/Health_Information/healthcare.php
(f): The Government is aware that during the Nipah virus outbreak reported in West Bengal
in early 2026, Singapore and Thailand had introduced temporary public health screening,
including temperature screening, at airports and seaports for travellers arriving from the
affected areas in India. These measures were implemented for a limited period and were
subsequently discontinued.
*****

ANNEXURE
The control measures undertaken and contingency plans for prevention and
containment of Nipah virus disease outbreaks:
i. Ministry of Health & Family Welfare (MoHFW) maintained continued support and
collaborative engagement with both Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratories
throughout the year, ensuring training, a steady supply of Personal protective equipment
and diagnostic reagents.
ii. Integrated Disease Surveillance Program (IDSP) mandates surveillance & response to
outbreak prone communicable diseases. IDSP plays a crucial role in prompt response and
surveillance of emerging and re-emerging diseases including Nipah Virus disease in the
country.
iii. Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and ICMR- National Institute of Virology,
Pune, have strengthened Nipah surveillance by enhancing Acute Encephalitis Syndrome
in Kerala state and Severe Acute Respiratory Illness surveillance in West Bengal and
Kerala since October-November 2024.
iv. A comprehensive guideline on Nipah Virus has been prepared which can be accessed on
the link: https://ncdc.mohfw.gov.in/nipah-virus-guidelines/.

paramedical staff and faculty in Government hospitals and medical colleges and the number

with the reasons therefor;

in rural/underserved areas and if so, the details thereof;
(c) the steps taken by the Government to fill these vacancies including recruitment drives
undertaken during the last five years, contractual appointments, and incentives for service in
rural and remote areas; and

resources in public healthcare institutions and if so, the details thereof?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND

healthcare system, including vacancies lies with the respective State/Union Territory
Governments. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare provides technical and financial
support to the States/Union Territory to strengthen the public healthcare system in rural areas
based on the proposals received in the form of Programme Implementation Plans (PIPs)
under National Health Mission. Government of India provides approval for the proposal in
the form of Record of Proceedings (RoPs) as per norms & available resources.

The NHM supplements the regular human resources by filling up the gaps in human

62.pdf

doctors and healthcare workers to practice in rural and remote areas of the country to mitigate
the impact of shortage of doctors and healthcare workers:
• Hard area allowance to specialist doctors for serving in rural and remote areas and for
their residential quarters so that they find it attractive to serve in public health
facilities in such areas.
• Honorarium to Gynaecologists/ Emergency Obstetric Care (EmOC) trained,
Pediatricians & Anesthetist/ Life Saving Anaesthesia Skills (LSAS) trained doctors is

Midwife (ANM) for ensuring timely Antenatal Checkup (ANC) checkup and
recording, incentives for conducting Adolescent Reproductive and Sexual Health
activities.
• States are also allowed to offer negotiable salary to attract specialist including
flexibility in strategies such as “You Quote We Pay”.
• Non-Monetary incentives such as preferential admission in post graduate courses for
staff serving in difficult areas and improving accommodation arrangement in rural
areas have also been introduced under NHM.
• Multi-skilling of doctors is supported under NHM to overcome the shortage of
specialists. Skill upgradation of existing HR is another major strategy under NRHM
for achieving improvement in health outcomes.

The measures/steps taken by the Government to increase the doctors/medical
professionals in the country includes:-
• Centrally Sponsored Scheme for establishment of new medical college by upgrading
district/ referral hospital under which 157 medical colleges have been approved.
• Centrally Sponsored Scheme for strengthening/ upgradation of existing State
Government/Central Government Medical Colleges to increase MBBS and PG seats.
• DNB qualification has been recognized for appointment as faculty to take care of
shortage of faculty.
• Enhancement of age limit for appointment/ extension/ re-employment against posts of
teachers/Dean/Principal/ Director in medical colleges upto 70 years.

curriculum to provide equitable healthcare access to rural population. FAP involves

ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF PORTS, SHIPPING & WATERWAYS 
(SHRI SARBANANDA SONOWAL) 
  
(a) to (d) In view of the evolving maritime security situation, the Directorate General of 
Maritime Administration (DGMA), a subordinate body under this Ministry progressively 
updates its advisories in response to the evolving security situation across the region. 
Advisories are precautionary in nature and are intended to enhance the safety and 
security of lndian seafarers. They were issued in response to the evolving security 
situation and not to any single incident.    
Further, from the onset of the security situation in the Strait of Hormuz, several 
measures have been taken to safeguard lndian seafarers. These include the 
establishment of a dedicated 24x7 Control Room, maintenance of a live vessel-and-
crew database, and issuance of a Situation Report (SITREP) every 24 hours (currently 
SITREP No. 165) to monitor the movement of vessels, lndian seafarers, incidents and 
casualties. DGMA has also developed an integrated digital platform with dedicated 
24x7 Marine Casualty Reporting, Crisis Management and Seafarer Grievance 
Redressal modules to ensure prompt reporting and response. The evolving maritime 

security situation is being continuously monitored through the DG Communication 
Centre (DGCOMM) in coordination with the Indian Navy, Flag States, coastal 
authorities, shipowners, ship managers, Recruitment and Placement Services Licence 
(RPSL) agencies and other concerned stakeholders. The details are placed at 
Annexure. 
   
  
  

Annexure 
  
(1)  Round-the-clock monitoring, reporting and crisis-response backbone 
  
(i)        DG Communication Centre (MMDAC) – the central maritime distress 
and coordination node, manned 24x7, together with a dedicated 24-hour 
Control Room.  
  
(ii)        Daily ship reporting advisory – vessels in the region report through the 
online Ship Reporting Form, maintaining a live vessel-and-crew database. 
  
(iii)       Continuous real-time monitoring – through the DGComm Centre, with a 
Situation Report issued every 24 hours (currently SITREP No. 165) to track 
vessels, seafarers, incidents and casualties. 
  
(iv)      eNavik Portal – an integrated digital platform with dedicated 24x7 Marine 
Casualty Reporting, Crisis Management and Seafarer Grievance Redressal 
modules, providing digital incident reporting with automated routing to the 
concerned authorities and real-time tracking of response measures. 
  
(2)       Whole-of-government and international coordination 
  
(i)        Inter-agency coordination is maintained by DGMA/ Ministry of Ports, 
Shipping & Waterways with the Ministry of External Affairs, the Indian Navy, the 
Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, the Department of Fertilizers, the IFC-IOR 
and Indian Missions abroad. 
  
(ii)    International coordination – evacuation of stranded seafarers is pursued 
through a coordinated mechanism involving the IMO, the UKMTO, the MICA 
Centre and coastal States. 
  
  
(3)       Evacuation and repatriation 
As on 03 August 2026, 4052 seafarers have been repatriated from the Gulf 
region and 62 vessels have successfully transited Strait of Hormuz (23 Indian-
flagged and 39 foreign-flagged) for India. 
  
(4)      RPSL / e-migration system 
 
Single point of control – every Indian seafarer is engaged through a licensed 
RPSL agency and cannot clear e-migration or sign on to a vessel without 
formal, verified approval.  
  
(5)       Welfare and Assistance

affected seafarers is maintained.

988-0256; WhatsApp +91 8655856830; email enavik.24x7@gov.in; and 
the e-Navik grievance portal.

PREVENTIVE HEALTHCARE AND SCREENING PROGRAMMES
†3252. SHRI GYANESHWARPATIL:
Will the Minister OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the current status of early screening programmes for diabetes, hypertension and major cancers in
primary and secondary healthcare facilities across the country;
(b) the extent to which nutrition education has been institutionalised under public health initiatives and
the details thereof;
(c) the steps taken by the Government in coordination with other Ministries, to tackle air pollution and
ensure access to safe drinking water as preventive health interventions; and
(d) whether any cost-benefit assessment has been conducted to compare the expenditure on preventive
healthcare with the expenditure on tertiary healthcare and ICU infrastructure along with its findings
and the action taken by the Government thereon, along with the details regarding the State of Madhya
Pradesh?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAO JADHA V)
(a) to (d): The Department of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India provides technical and
financial support to the States and Union Territories under the National Programme for Prevention and
Control of Non-Communicable Diseases (NP-NCD). Under NP-NCD, 770 District NCD Clinics, 233
Cardiac Care Units and 6,410 NCD clinics at Community Health Centres have been set up across the
country. In addition, 524 Day Care Cancer Centres (DCCCs) are functional across the country to
ensure cancer care accessibility at district level.
A population-based initiative for prevention, control and screening for common NCDs i.e. diabetes,
hypertension, oral, breast and cervical cancer was rolled out in the country under National Health
Mission (NHM) as a part of Comprehensive Primary Health Care. Under the initiative, persons more
than 30 years of age are targeted for screening. Till July 2026, 42.4 crore have been screened for
hypertension, 42.21 crore for diabetes, 36.11
crore for oral cancer, 16.94 crore for breast cancer and 9.31 crore for cervical cancer as per the
National NCD Portal.
Nutrition education has been institutionalised as an integral component of public health initiatives
under the National Health Mission (NHM) and POSHAN Abhiyaan across the country including
Madhya Pradesh. A lifecycle approach is adopted to provide nutrition education and counselling
through AyushmanArogya Mandirs (AAMs), Village Health, Sanitation and Nutrition Days (VHSNDs),
and community-based platforms. Under POSHAN Abhiyaan, implemented in convergence with the
Ministry of Women & Child Development, behaviour change communication is promoted through the
Jan Andolan approach, supported by nutrition e-learning modules developed by ICMR–National

Institute of Nutrition (NIN). Nutrition education is further strengthened through Rashtriya Bal Swasthya
Karyakram (RBSK), Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram (RKSK) and the Eat Right India initiative.
These interventions are implemented uniformly across all States and Union Territories, including
Madhya Pradesh.
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has launched the National Clean Air Programme
(NCAP) in 2019 to address issues related to air pollution. Ministry of Jal Shakti in partnership with
States is implementing Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) – Har Ghar Jal to provide potable water to every
rural household of the country through functional tap water connection.
Preventive aspect of NCDs is strengthened under Comprehensive Primary Health Care through
Ayushman Arogya Mandir, by promotion of wellness activities and targeted communication at the
community level across the country including including Madhya Pradesh. Further initiatives for
increasing public awareness about NCDs and for promotion of healthy lifestyle includes observation
of National & International Health Days and use of print, electronic and social media for continued
community awareness. In addition, the Fit India Movement promotes regular physical activity and
healthy living, while the Khelo India programme encourages sports and fitness among all age groups.
Various Yoga-related activities are also undertaken by the Ministry of AYUSH to promote health and
wellness.

One Nation One Fertilizer Initiative 
 
†3259. Shri Damodar Agrawal: 
Shri Dilip Saikia: 
Shri Anil Firojiya: 
Shri Bhojraj Nag: 
Shri Vijay Baghel: 
Shri Alok Sharma: 
Shri Suresh Kumar Kashyap: 
Shri Chandra Prakash Joshi: 
Shri Trivendra Singh Rawat: 
 
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state: 
(a) the extent to which avoidable inter-State transportation of fertilizers, 
transportation cost and supply bottlenecks have been reduced through the One 
Nation One Fertilizer alongwith the benefits accrued to the farmers therefrom; 
(b)  whether the Government proposes to further strengthen the availability, storage 
capacity and distribution network of the Bharat brand fertilizers in the country, if 
so, the details thereof, State/district-wise including Himachal Pradesh, 
particularly in Shimla Parliamentary Constituency; and  
(c) the statistical data regarding the demand, supply and seamless distribution of 
fertilizers of Bharat brand to farmers under the said initiative during the last two 
years, fertilizer-wise and State/district-wise including Rajasthan, particularly in 
Chittorgarh Parliamentary Constituency? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
 (SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
 
(a) One Nation One Fertilizer scheme stands implemented under “Pradhanmantri 
Bhartiya Janurvarak Pariyojna” (PMBJP) with effect from 24th August, 2022. All fertilizers 
companies viz Public sector, Cooperative and Private sector are required to sell 
subsidized fertilizers under brand name “BHARAT” across the country. The objective of 
the scheme is to increase the availability basket of fertilizers; take care of dilemma 
among farmers in choosing from plethora of brands manufactured by various companies 
available in the markets, reduce the crisscross movement and further ensure timely 
supply of fertilizers across the country. By consolidating branding under a single 
“BHARAT” brand, the scheme fosters transparency, combats malpractices, and ensures 
equitable access to essential nutrients for crops.  
 

(b) and (c) Following Steps are taken by the Government every season for ensuring 
timely and adequate supply of fertilizers across the States/UTs, including the States of 
Himachal Pradesh and Rajasthan: 
i. Before the commencement of each cropping season, Department of Agriculture 
and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with all the State Governments, 
assesses the State-wise & month-wise requirement of fertilizers. On the basis 
of requirement projected by DA&FW, Department of Fertilizers (DoF) allocates 
adequate quantities of fertilizers to States by issuing monthly supply plan and 
continuously monitors the availability. 
ii. The movement of all major subsidized fertilizers is monitored throughout the 
country by an on-line web-based monitoring system called integrated Fertilizer 
Management System (iFMS). 
iii. The gap between demand (requirement) and production for Urea & other 
fertilizer is met through imports. The import for the season is also finalized well 
in advance to ensure timely availability.  
iv. The State Governments are regularly advised to coordinate with manufacturers 
and importers for streamlining the supplies through timely placement of indents. 
v. Regularly coordinate with the Ministry of Railways for giving sufficient rakes, 
priority to fertilizers and for timely evacuation of rakes for States. 
vi. The distribution of fertilizers within the State at district level is done by the 
concerned State government. 
Accordingly, the availability of fertilizers i.e. Urea, DAP, MOP and NPKS has 
remained adequate across the States/UTs, including the States of Himachal Pradesh 
and Rajasthan, during the last two years (i.e. in FYs 2024-25 to 2025-26). The 
information regarding requirement, availability and sales of these fertilizers across the 
States/UTs, including the States of Himachal Pradesh and Rajasthan, during the said 
period is placed at Annexure.

†3260. SMT. SANDHYARAY:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government has formulated any time-bound national action plan to ensure the
equitable availability of quality and specialised health services in every Parliamentary
Constituency in the country;
(b) if so, the details of the amount sanctioned, year-wise expenditure and the current progress
on these projects from 2014 till date;
(c) if not, the future action plan of the Government for strengthening health facilities in such
Parliamentary Constituencies, including the Bhind and Datia; and
(d) the details of medical colleges, nursing colleges, Critical Care Blocks, District Hospital
upgradation, health and wellness centres and other health infrastructure projects sanctioned
under the said action plan in the country, State-wise, particularly in Madhya Pradesh and
specifically in Bhind and Datia Parliamentary Constituencies?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) to (d): ‘Public Health’ & ‘Hospitals’ are State subjects. The primary responsibility of the
availability of quality and specialised health services in the country lies with the respective
State Governments.
The National Health Mission (NHM) provides support for improvement in health
infrastructure, human resources in health facilities, availability and accessibility to quality
healthcare across the country including Madhya Pradesh. The Ministry of Health and Family
Welfare (MoHFW) provides technical and financial support to the States/UTs to strengthen
the public healthcare system, based on the proposals received in the form of Programme
Implementation Plans (PIPs) under NHM. Approval is accorded to the proposals in the form
of Record of Proceedings (RoPs) as per norms & available resources. The details of RoPs
issued to States/UTs including Madhya Pradesh are available at following web link:
https://nhm.gov.in/index1.php?lang=1&level=1&sublinkid=1377&lid=744

National Quality Assurance Standards (NQAS), launched by Government of India, provides a
comprehensive framework aimed at enhancing the quality of care in public health facilities by
focusing on areas such as service provision, patient rights, inputs, support services, clinical
care, infection control, quality management. This lead to better patient outcomes and
increased public trust in healthcare services.
Health Dynamics of India (HDI), is an annual publication, based on healthcare administrative
data reported by States/UTs. Details of availability of medical colleges, District Hospitals
(DHs) and other health infrastructure across the country including Bhind and Datia
Parliamentary Constituencies of Madhya Pradesh, State/UT-wise, may be accessed through
the HMIS portal under Publications at the following link of HDI 2023-24:
https://hmis.mohfw.gov.in
As reported by States/UTs on AAM portal, 1,86,696 AAMs including 12,789 AAMs in
Madhya Pradesh, were operationalized by strengthening Sub-health Centres (SHCs) and
Primary Health Centres (PHCs) in the country, as on 31.07.2026. Out of these, 258 AAMs in
Bhind district and 141 AAMs in Datia district of Bhind and Datia Parliamentary
Constituencies were operationalized.
Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM) is a Centrally
Sponsored Scheme (CSS) with certain Central Sector (CS) components, which was
implemented to strengthen India's public health system through reforms that integrate health
service delivery, public health action and health research, thereby enhancing the capacity of
public health systems to effectively respond to pandemics and other public health emergencies.
Under CSS component of the scheme, administrative approvals were accorded to the
States/UTs under PM-ABHIM for 5 years’ period i.e. FY2021-22 to FY 2025-26 for an
amount of Rs. 32,961.10 crore for construction/ strengthening and establishment of 11001
Building-less Sub-Health Centre – Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (SHC-AAMs), 5456 Urban
Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (Urban-AAMs), 2151 Block Public Health Units (BPHUs), 744
Integrated Public Health Laboratories (IPHLs) and 631 Critical Care Blocks (CCBs) at
District Hospitals/Government Medical College level, including 50 CCBs in Madhya Pradesh
(1 each in Bhind and Datia district).
MoHFW administers a CSS for 'Establishment of new medical colleges attached with existing
district/referral hospitals' with preference to underserved areas and aspirational districts,
where there is no existing Government or private medical college. Under the Scheme, all the
envisaged 157 Government medical colleges have already been approved in the country
including 14 in Madhya Pradesh. One medical college at Datia was approved. Under CSS for
Aug

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
DEPARTMENT OF FERTILIZERS 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3261 TO BE ANSWERED ON: 07.08.2026 
 
Availability and Accessibility of Fertilizers 
 
3261. Shri Vishnu Datt Sharma: 
            
Will the Minister of Chemicals and Fertilizers be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has made any assessment regarding fertiliser 
availability and accessibility, under the Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS), Urea Subsidy 
and One Nation One Fertilizer initiatives in Bundelkhand region, if so, the details thereof, 
district-wise, particularly Khajuraho Constituency; 
 
(b) whether the delays in fertiliser supply, inadequate storage and long travel 
distances to fertiliser outlets have affected farmers during the short Kharif and Rabi 
sowing windows, if so, the details thereof, district-wise; 
 
(c)  whether the Government proposes a Bundelkhand Fertiliser Logistics Plan 
including block-level buffer stocks, advance seasonal allocation, strengthened rural 
distribution and promotion of balanced fertiliser use; and 
 
(d)  if so, the details thereof alongwith timeline for its implementation? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS 
 
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
 
 
(a) to (e) Following steps are taken by the Government every season for ensuring 
timely and adequate availability of fertilizers in the country, including Bundelkhand region: 
 
(i) Before the commencement of each cropping season, Department of Agriculture 
and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with all the State Governments, 
assesses the State-wise & month-wise requirement of fertilizers. On the basis of 
requirement projected by DA&FW, Department of Fertilizers (DoF) allocates 
adequate quantities of fertilizers to States by issuing monthly supply plan and 
continuously monitors the availability. 
 
(ii) The movement of all major subsidized fertilizers is monitored throughout the 
country by an on-line web-based monitoring system called integrated Fertilizer 
Management System (iFMS). 

 
(iii) The gap between demand (requirement) and production for Urea & other 
fertilizers is met through imports. The import for the season is also finalized well 
in advance to ensure timely availability.  
 
(iv) The State Governments are regularly advised to coordinate with manufacturers 
and importers for streamlining the supplies through timely placement of indents. 
 
(v) Regular coordination is done with the Ministry of Railways for giving sufficient 
rakes, priority to fertilizers and for timely evacuation of rakes for States. 
 
(vi) The distribution of fertilizers within the State at district/block level is done by the 
concerned State government. 
 
In view of above, the availability of fertilizers viz. Urea, DAP, MOP and NPKS has 
remained adequate in the Bundelkhand region in the Rabi 2025-26 season and during 
the ongoing Kharif 2026 season. The information regarding availability position of 
fertilizers in the Bundelkhand region during the ongoing Kharif 2026 season, as informed 
by State Governments of Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, is placed at Annexure. 
 
Further, the State Government of Madhya Pradesh has informed that they make 
arrangements for distribution of fertilizers through PACS, MARKFED, MP Agro and 
authorized private dealers. The distribution of fertilizers is also being monitored through 
the E-Vikas (Distribution and Agricultural Fertilizer Supply Solution) system, which 
provides for monitoring of fertilizer movement from the source/production point up to the 
retailer level and for distribution according to farmers' land and crop requirements.  In 
respect of the Khajuraho Parliamentary Constituency, fertilizer availability is being 
monitored through the concerned district administration and agriculture/cooperative 
machinery.  
 
Moreover, the State Governments of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh have 
informed that at present, there is no separate proposal under consideration for a formally 
notified “Bundelkhand Fertilizer Logistics Plan” as a standalone scheme.

entries.t: Multilateral Response to the Global Energy Crisis
entries.head:
1
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFARIS
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 3262
ANSWERED ON- 07/08/2026
MULTILATERAL RESPONSE TO THE GLOBAL ENERGY CRISIS
3262 SHRI DUSHYANT SINGH
Will the Minister of External Affairs be pleased to state:-
(a) the recent initiatives undertaken by India through platforms such  
as  the  G20,  BRICS,  SCO  and  the  Voice  of  Global  South  Summit 
(VOGSS) to strengthen multilateralism and deepen cooperation among 
countries of  the Global South in the context of  the recent energy  
disruptions arising from the conflict in West Asia;
(b)  the  steps  taken  by  Government  to  build  consensus  among 
developing countries on issues of  energy security, resilient supply  
chains, food and fertilizer security and climate-resilient development,  
particularly in light of  the disruptions in global oil and LNG flows  
through the Strait of Hormuz;

2
(c)  whether  Government  has  initiated  or  proposed  any  collective 
South-South cooperation mechanism for strategic energy reserves,  
renewable energy partnerships and crisis-response coordination to  
support developing countries affected by the present crisis, if so, the  
details thereof; and
(d) the manner in which these initiatives further India’s vision of  a  
more  inclusive,  representative  and  resilient  multilateral  order  
reflecting the priorities of the Global South?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS
(SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA)
(a) to (d): India has consistently worked to strengthen multilateralism  
and deepen cooperation among countries of the Global South through  
platforms such as the G20, BRICS, SCO and the Voice of Global South  
Summit,  including  on  concerns  arising  from  recent  disruptions  in 
global energy markets.  India advocates greater cooperation among  
developing countries on energy security, food and fertilizer security,  

3
resilient supply chains, while safeguarding developmental priorities.  
India  engages  with  partner  countries  through  bilateral  and  
multilateral  mechanisms,  to  exchange  views,  build  consensus  and 
support coordinated approaches aimed at mitigating adverse impacts  
on  developing  economies  in  the  context  of  the  recent  energy 
disruptions,  as  also  fostering  discussions  on   renewable  energy 
partnerships, clean energy transitions, capacity building and sharing  
of technology. 
India assumed the BRICS Chairship in 2026 under the overarching  
theme  "Building  for  Resilience,  Innovation,  Cooperation  and  
Sustainability".  Resilience  is  one  of  the  substantive  pillars  of  the 
Chairship under which deliberations on resilience of energy systems,  
supply chains and infrastructure are taking place.  India is actively  
engaged in the discussions in G20 this year on matters relating to  
energy supply, diversification of energy sources and systems, greater  
investment  in  energy  infrastructure,  and  increasing  resilience  of 
energy supply chains, while safeguarding the developmental priorities  
and policy space of developing countries.

4
India's  international  initiatives,  including  the  International  Solar 
Alliance  and  the  Global  Biofuels Alliance,  promote  clean  energy 
deployment, energy access, capacity building and sustainable energy  
transitions, contributing to South–South energy cooperation and to  
ensuring that the concerns and development priorities of the Global  
South are placed on the agenda of global decision-making processes.  
These initiatives contribute to India's consistent advocacy of a more  
inclusive, representative, equitable and resilient multilateral order.  
The inclusion of the African Union as a permanent member of the G20  
during India's Presidency, and the expansion of BRICS membership,  
reflect India's sustained efforts to widen representation of developing  
countries in global decision-making.

in Gujarat from January 2023 to May 2026;
(b) the details of the empanelment of public and private hospitals under AB-PMJAY in
Tier-II and Tier-III towns and tribal areas of the said constituency;
(c) the number of Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (AAMs) operational in the said constituency
and the progress made towards creating Ayushman Bharat Health Accounts (ABHA) for rural
people; and
(d) the specific data regarding the rate of hospitalisation for women and the estimated
reduction in out-of-pocket medical expenditure for families in the said constituency since the
inception of AB-PMJAY?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND
FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) and (b): The constituency-wise data is not captured under Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan
Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY), however, the district-wise details of Ayushman
Cards created in the districts under the Dahod Lok Sabha Constituency can be accessed at:
https://dashboard.nha.gov.in/public/card
Further, a total of 73,021 hospital admissions in Dahod District and a total of 38,270 hospital
admissions in Mahisagar District of Dahod Lok Sabha constituency have been authorised
under the scheme from January 2023 to May 2026.
The district-wise details of the of public and private hospitals empanelled under the scheme
can be accessed at: https://hem.nha.gov.in/search

(c): Through 1.86 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandir (AAM), comprehensive primary healthcare
is provided by strengthening Sub Health Centres and Primary Health Centres. As per the
AAM Portal as on 30.06.2026, the number of operational AAM in the State of Gujarat is
10625 including 528 and 227 in Dahod and Mahisagar districts, respectively.
Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) is a key building block of Ayushman Bharat
Digital Mission (ABDM). It is a unique 14-digit health identifier which allows citizens to
securely access and manage their digital health records across the healthcare ecosystem.
While creating ABHA, only district-level details are captured based on the address details
available in Aadhaar, and rural-urban bifurcation of ABHA creation is not maintained under
ABDM. As on 31.07.2026, a total of 8.60 lakh and 17.93 lakh ABHA have been created in
the Mahisagar & Dahod districts respectively falling under the Dahod Parliamentary
Constituency in the State of Gujarat.
(d): As on 31.07.2026, a total of 1.34 lakh hospital admissions, amounting to Rs.285.99 crore
were authorised under AB-PMJAY in Dahod district. In Mahisagar district, 68,167 hospital
admissions, amounting to Rs.187.71 crore, were authorised during the same period. Of these,
63,917 admissions in Dahod district, constituting 47.7 % of the total admissions and
amounting to Rs.113.51 crore, pertained to eligible female beneficiaries. Similarly, in
Mahisagar district, 29,327 admissions, constituting 43.02% of the total admissions and
amounting to Rs. 70.82 crore, pertained to eligible female beneficiaries.
By providing eligible beneficiary families with cashless access to secondary and tertiary
healthcare services at empanelled hospitals, the scheme has significantly reduced the
financial burden associated with hospitalization and provided protection against catastrophic
health expenditure.

3267. Shri Brijmohan Agrawal:   
 Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state: 
(a) the total requirement of elemental sulphur in the country during FY 2025-26 
alongwith details of major sectors in which elemental sulphur is consumed; 
(b) the details of sulphur imports during last five years, including the quantity 
imported from each country, country-wise; 
(c) the details of major Indian companies that imported sulphur along with the 
quantity imported by each such company during the financial year 2025-26, 
country-wise; 
(d) whether there is a shortage in sulphur supply on account of the ongoing 
conflict/tensions in West Asia, if so, the details thereof; 
(e) the steps taken by the Government to meet domestic sulphur demand in 
view of the prevailing West Asia crisis; and 
(f) whether the Government is exploring diversification of sulphur import sources 
to other countries and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
 
(a) & (b):  The total estimated annual requirement of sulphur in Phosphatic & Potassic 
(P&K) fertilizer industry is 30-35 lakh metric tonne. Sulphur is also consumed in non-
fertilizer sectors including chemicals (sulphuric acid, dyes, and intermediates), 
petroleum refining, metal processing, rubber industry, and other industrial applications. 
The country-wise details of sulphur imports during last five years, including the quantity 
imported from each country is placed at Annexure. 
 

(c): As per the policy of the Directorate General of Commercial Intelligence and 
Statistics (DGCI&S) company-wise details of sulphur imports are sensitive and are not 
disclosed. 
 
(d) to (f): In view of the ongoing conflict/tensions in West Asia, there have been 
disruptions in global supply chains, leading to increased freight costs, insurance 
premiums, and shipment delays. The Government is monitoring the availability of 
sulphur in fertilizer sector, the matter been has taken up with the Ministry of Petroleum 
and Natural Gas (MoPNG) to advise PSU and private sector refineries to prioritize 
supply of sulphur to the fertilizer sector, in view of its critical importance for production 
of phosphatic fertilizers.  
Further, the Government has implemented Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) 
Scheme w.e.f. 01.04.2010 for Phosphatic and Potassic (P&K) Fertilizers. Under the 
Scheme, P&K fertilizers are covered under Open General License (OGL) and 
companies are free to import/manufacture these fertilizers/raw materials including 
sulphur as per their business dynamics.

entries.t: Lack of Transparency in Pharmaceutical Sector
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
DEPARTMENT OF PHARMACEUTICALS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3268 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 7th AUGUST, 2026 
 
Lack of Transparency in Pharmaceutical Sector 
 
3268. Dr. M K Vishnu Prasad:  
 
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of the lack of transparency in the pharmaceutical 
sector regarding production costs, pricing, trade margins and profit on medicines, if so, the 
details thereof;  
(b) whether any action has been taken against pharmaceutical companies found indulging in 
overpricing, unethical profiteering or violation of drug pricing norms, if so, the details thereof;  
(c) whether the Government has made any assessment regarding the impact of excessive 
marketing and promotional expenditure by pharmaceutical companies on the prices of 
medicines, if so, the details thereof;  
(d) whether the Government proposes to regulate or cap such marketing and promotional 
expenses to make essential medicines more affordable, if so, the details thereof; and  
(e) the plans for international best practices and regulations to ensure that healthcare and 
medicines remain affordable and accessible to all citizens in the country? 
 
ANSWER  
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND 
FERTILIZERS 
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
 
(a): Prices of drugs are regulated as per the provisions of the Drugs (Prices Control) Order 
2013 (DPCO, 2013 ) which has been promulgated based on the principles of the National 
Pharmaceutical Pricing Policy, 2012 (“NPPP, 2012”). National Pharmaceutical Pricing 
Authority (NPPA) fixes ceiling prices of formulations specified in Schedule -I to DPCO, 
2013 in accordance with the provisions of DPCO  based on market data  and retail price of a 
new drug as defined under 2(1)(u) of DPCO, 2013 that is applicable to the applicant 
manufacturer and marketer, who are required to sell the new drug within the price notified by 
NPPA. In case of non-scheduled formulations, a manufacturer is required to not increase MRP 
of a non-scheduled drug by more than 10% of MRP during the preceding 12 months.   
 
As a transparency measure, a draft version of the price calculation sheets for the 
proposed revised price notifications, are uploaded on the website of NPPA for 10 working days 
to invite comments from stakeholders. Only after taking into account comments re ceived and 
any additional data received within the said time period, NPPA finalises ceiling and retail 
prices. Thus, the entire procedure of price fixation is available in the public domain, which 
ensures transparency and accountability of the process. All price notifications issued by NPPA 
are available on its website (https://nppa.gov.in). 

(b): NPPA monitors the compliance with the provisions of the DPCO, 2013 and takes 
appropriate action in cases of overcharging and other violations, in accordance with the 
provisions of DPCO, 2013, based on references received from various sources, including Price 
Monitoring and Resource Units set up in States, State Drugs Controllers, samples purchased 
from open market, reports from market database and complaints lodged through various 
grievance redress channels . In addition , to prevent overpricing, DPCO 2013 requires every 
manufacturer of a formulation to print the maximum retail price on the label of the container 
of such formulation. Further, no person is permitted to sell any formulation to any consumer at 
a price exceeding the price specified on the current price list or price indicated on the label of 
the container or the pack thereof, whichever is less.  
 
(c) and (d): With the aim to prevent unethical marketing and ensuring responsible promotion 
of pharmaceutical products by regulating interactions between doctors / registered medical 
practitioners (RMPs) and representatives of pharmaceutical companies, the DoP, on 12.3.2024, 
has issued the Uniform Code of Pharmaceuticals Marketing Practices 2024. The code outlines 
guidelines regarding promotion of drugs among doctors/RMPs. Pharmaceutical companies are 
accountable for the actions of their medical representatives  and other employees. The code 
prohibits provision of gifts, monetary benefits and hospitality to doctors and their family 
members by pharmaceutical companies. It includes requirements for pharmaceutical 
companies to self -declare adherence to the code and disclose expenditures related to 
conferences, seminars and workshops organised for continuing medical education and 
continuing professional development. Companies may undergo independent, random or risk -
based audits. The code establishes a two -layer complaint adjudication process, with appeals 
handled by the Department of Pharmaceuticals. Penalties under the code include the following:  
 
(i) Reprimand to the pharmaceutical entity and publication of full details thereof;  
(ii) Recovery of money or items given

MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS 
DEPARTMENT OF FERTILIZERS 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UN-STARRED Question No. 3269 TO BE ANSWERED ON 07.08.2026 
 
Impact of Neem-Coated Urea 
 
3269. Shri Mahendra Singh Solanky: 
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has made neem-coating of urea mandatory across the 
country, if so, the details and the objectives thereof; 
(b) the benefits achieved through neem-coated urea in improving nitrogen-use 
efficiency, reducing fertilizer misuse and enhancing crop productivity, 
particularly for farmers of the Dewas–Shajapur Parliamentary Constituency of 
Madhya Pradesh; 
(c) whether the Government has made any assessment regarding the impact of 
neem-coated urea in preventing diversion of subsidized urea for industrial and 
other non-agricultural purposes, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the quantity of neem-coated urea produced, supplied and marketed during the 
last three years, along with the details of allocation and distribution made to the 
State including the said Constituency, year-wise? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS 
 
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
 
(a) to (c): It is mandatory for all the domestic producers and importers of Urea to supply 
100% Neem Coated Urea (NCU) since 2015 onwards.One of the primary benefits of 
Neem Coating is that due to slow release, the consumption of NCU reduces as compared 
to normal Urea, improving crop uptake, and reducing environmental losses. Research 
findings indicated that the average yield enhancement due to use of NCU is 8.25%. 
Further, application of NCU, significantly reduced the nitrogen losses by about 10%-15%. 
Neem-Coated Urea (NCU) acts as an effective nitrification inhibitors, leading to higher 
soil NH4+-N and lower NO2-N compared to prilled Urea, though their performance varies 
with soil type, crop, and region. Several studies have shown that NCU increases nitrogen 

availability, reduces NO3 leaching, and minimizes NH3 volatilization losses. Research 
across different soils consistently reports higher nitrogen recovery, improved yield at 
lower N application rates, and reduced nitrogen losses. 
The Government of India in consultation with the State Government is regularly 
monitoring the enforcement action taken by State Government against the cases of Black 
marketing, Hoarding, Sub-standard and Diversion on weekly basis. In the country, Since 
April 2026, 1,69,031 raids have been conducted with 9,127 show cause notices issued, 
2,868 licenses suspended/cancelled and 270 FIRs registered against defaulters. 
Additionally, in case of diversion 414 show cause notices issued, 113 licenses 
suspended/cancelled and 46 FIRs registered. This Ministry regularly pursue with the 
State Government to strictly implement the enforcement action against the defaulters. 
(d): The Quantum of Neem Coated Urea produced in the country during the last three 
years is as under: 
Year Production of Neem-Coated Urea (Fig. in LMT) 
2023-24 314.06 
2024-25 306.41

Source: dbfert.nic.in 
In addition, following steps are taken by the Government every season for ensuring timely 
and adequate supply of fertilizers across the States/UTs, including the State of Madhya 
Pradesh: 
I. Before the commencement of each cropping season, Department of Agriculture 
and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with all the State Governments, 
assesses the State-wise& month-wise requirement of fertilizers. On the basis of 
requirement projected by DA&FW, Department of Fertilizers (DoF) allocates 
adequate quantities of fertilizers to States by issuing monthly supply plan and 
continuously monitors the availability. 
II. The movement of all major subsidized fertilizers is monitored throughout the 
country by an on-line web-based monitoring system called integrated Fertilizer 
Management System (iFMS). 
III. The gap between demand (requirement) and production for Urea & other fertilizer 
is met through imports. The import for the season is also finalized well in advance 
to ensure timely availability.  
IV. The State Governments are regularly advised to coordinate with manufacturers 
and importers for streamlining the supplies through timely placement of indents. 
V. Regularly coordinate with the Ministry of Railways for giving sufficient rakes, 
priority to fertilizers and for timely evacuation of rakes for States. 

VI. The distribution of fertilizers within the State at district level is done by the 
concerned State government. 
Accordingly, the availability of Urea has remained adequate in the State of Madhya 
Pradesh during the last three years (i.e. in FYs 2023-24 to 2025-26). The information 
regarding requirement, availability and sales of Urea in the State during the said period 
is placed at Annexure.

3270. SHRI RAHUL GANDHI:
Will the Minister of HEALTHAND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the reasons for the rising cases of food adulteration, contamination, counterfeiting and
repeated violations of food safety standards across the country;
(b) the details of food samples tested and found unsafe, prosecutions launched, convictions
secured, and the number of deaths due to food adulteration during the last five years, year
wise and State-wise;
(c) the details of food-testing infrastructure, including the number of functional laboratories,
the average testing time and vacancies of Food Safety Officers, State-wise;
(d) the number of notified FSSAI laboratories lacking facilities to test for heavy metals,
pesticide residues and bacterial contamination, along with the reasons therefor;
(e) whether any regulatory framework specifically governs storage conditions, temperature
control, hygiene, traceability and inspection frequency at quick-commerce dark stores, if so,
the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and
(f) whether the Government proposes to launch a comprehensive National Food Safety
Mission to ensure food traceability, strengthen surveillance and safeguard public health, if so,
the details thereof?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) to (f): Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) is mandated to lay down
science-based standards for articles of food and to regulate their manufacture, storage,
distribution, sale and import to ensure availability of safe and wholesome food for human
consumption. The implementation and enforcement of the Food Safety and Standards (FSS) Act,
2006 is a shared responsibility between the Central and State Governments.

Around 98% of the Food Business Operators (FBOs) fall within the jurisdiction of the
State/UT Food Safety Authorities. Accordingly, the enforcement and implementation of the
provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (FSS Act, 2006) primarily rests with the
State/UT Food Safety Authorities within their respective jurisdictions. For compliance with the
standards, limits, and other statutory requirements prescribed under the Food Safety and
Standards Act, 2006, and the regulations made thereunder, the State Food Safety Authorities
undertake surveillance, monitoring, targeted enforcement drives, inspections, and sampling
activities across the food sector.
Details of enforcement action taken by the State/UT Food Safety Authorities against non
-conforming food products (including adulteration) during the last 5 years (state wise) are
placed at Annexure-I.
For the quality and safety of the food and food products, FSSAI has notified 259 NABL
accredited food testing laboratories for analysis of food samples and 24 Referral Food
Laboratories for the analysis of appellate samples. These laboratories are notified for analysis of
food samples in accordance with their NABL-accredited scope. The Food analyst is required to
submit the report of analysis within fourteen days of receipt of the sample. State-wise details of
food testing laboratories are placed at Annexure-II.
Matters related to vacancies of Food Safety Officers (FSOs) in states are taken up
regularly with the Commissioner of Food Safety of States/UTs through Central Advisory
Committee (CAC) meetings. State-wise details of sanctioned strength, actual strength and
vacancies of Food Safety Officers, are attached as Annexure-III.
The number of FSSAI notified laboratories lacking the facilities to test heavy metals,
pesticides, microbiological parameters etc. are 13 across the country. In order to upgrade and
strengthen the testing infrastructure of State Food Testing Laboratories (SFTL), FSSAI has
provided financial and technical assistance for establishment of facilities for microbiological
analysis and procurement of High End Equipment (HEE) for heavy metals and pesticide
residues analysis.
FSSAI has specified General Hygienic and Sanitary Practices to be followed by
Licensed/Registered Food Business Operators under Schedule 4 of FSS (Licensing and
Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011 which is applicable to all food business
operators including those involved in storage activity such as quick-commerce dark stores.
Schedule 4 of the said Regulations lays down the sanitary and hygienic requirements to be
complied with by Food Business Operators, including requirements relating to storage
conditions, temperature control, hygiene, transportation, pest control, personnel hygiene,
cleaning and sanitation, and maintenance of records to facilitate traceability, as applicable.

framework for arbitration. The Centre has also notified the India International Arbitra tion

Will the Minister of HEALTHAND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government is aware that a large number of patients suffering from end-stage
kidney failure remain on waiting lists for organ transplantation under programmes such as
Jeevandan and other organ allocation systems, resulting in avoidable deaths due to the
shortage of donor organs, if so, the details thereof;
(b) the number of patients currently awaiting kidney transplantation, the number of
transplants performed and the mortality reported among patients on waiting lists during the
last five years, year-wise and State-wise;
(c) whether the Government has assessed the gap between the demand for donor organs and
the availability of organs for transplantation, if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether the Government proposes to intensify nationwide awareness campaigns, simplify
organ donation procedures and strengthen hospital-based organ retrieval programmes to
increase deceased organ donation, if so, the details thereof; and
(e) the measures taken by the Government to reduce transplant waiting periods and encourage
voluntary organ donation to save lives and improve access to organ transplantation?

THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY

web portal https://notto.abdm.gov.in. As on date, more than 5 lakh Aadhaar verified pledges

In addition, a nationwide year-long public awareness campaign, “Jug Jug Jiyo Abhiyaan (जुग
जुग जजयो अजियान)” has been launched on 3rd August, 2026 with the aim to promote organ
and tissue donation. Further, the National Registry Portal has been upgraded and launched on

donation and transplantation processes, improve transparency and ensure smooth services to
the needy patients.

(a) whether the Government has assessed the disparities in access to quality and affordable
healthcare in Uttar Pradesh, particularly in the Sant Kabir Nagar and Ambedkar Nagar
districts and if so, the details thereof;
(b) the details of the sanctioned and vacant posts of doctors, specialists and paramedical

Life-saving Medicines 
 
†3274. Shri Hanuman Beniwal:  
Shri Rajkumar Roat:  
 
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that the increase in prices of essential and life -saving 
medicines has escalated the financial burden on common citizens, particularly patients 
belonging to low and middle-income groups and if so, the details of the price hike in medicines 
during the last three years, category-wise;  
(b) the steps taken by the Government to keep the prices of the said medicines affordable and 
to control unreasonable price increases during the last three years;  
(c) the number of cases of spurious, adulterated/Not of Standard Quality (NSQ) drugs that came 
to light in the country during the last three years, State-wise; and  
(d) the details of investigation, prosecution, license suspension/cancellation and other punitive 
actions taken by the Government against the concerned drug manufacturing companies, 
distributors and other defaulting entities in this regard? 
 
ANSWER  
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND 
FERTILIZERS 
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
 
(a) and (b): Prices of drugs are regulated as per the provisions of the Drugs (Prices Control) 
Order 2013 (DPCO, 2013). The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) under the 
Department of Pharmaceuticals regulates the prices of medicines as per extant provisio ns of 
DPCO, 2013. NPPA fixes the ceiling prices of formulations specified in Schedule-I to DPCO, 
2013 which is based on the National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM) published by 
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (Mo HFW) from time -to-time. As on 23.07.2026, 
Ceiling prices of 935 formulations are effective. The average price reduction due to refixation 
of prices under NLEM, 2022 is about 17%. NPPA also fixes retail prices of new drugs as 
defined in para 2(1)(u) of DPCO, 2013, i.e., formulatio ns launched by existing manufacturers 
of a medicine listed in NLEM by combining it with another drug, or by changing the strength 
or dosage or both of such medicine. The retail prices of new drugs are applicable to the 
applicant manufacturer and marketer and they cannot sell the new drug above the price notified 
by NPPA. Retail prices of 3,845 new drugs have been fixed by the NPPA till 23.07.2026. 
Further, in case of non-scheduled formulations, manufacturers are required to not increase the 
maximum retail p rice (MRP) of a formulation by more than ten percent of the MRP of that 

formulation during the preceding 12 months.  In addition, NPPA has fixed the prices of drugs 
under Para 19 to ensure the availability of drugs at affordable prices in public interest. Details 
of prices fixed or revised by NPPA are available on NPPA’s website (www.nppa.gov.in). 
 
The ceiling prices of scheduled medicines are revised annually on the basis of 
Wholesale Price Index (WPI) (all commodities) for preceding calendar year on or before 1 st 
April of every year, which is notified by the Government on the 1 st day of April every year. 
This notified increase is the maximum permissible increase for schedule drug for that year, and 
a manufacturer may avail the same or a lower increase in the price of such drugs. The WPI of 
the last 3 years are as follows: 
 
 
 
 
 
 
In case of non-scheduled formulations, manufacturers may avail an increase of up to 10 
per cent in the MRP of a formulation over the MRP of that formulation during the preceding 
12 months. However, it is observed from the market data (based on Pharmarack database for 
June, 2026) that the weighted average annual price increase in the non-scheduled drugs over 
the last three years is 6.94% which is below the permissible price increase of 10% p.a. 
 
NPPA monitors the prices of both scheduled and non -scheduled formulations on an 
ongoing basis and takes action in accordance with the provisions of DPCO, 2013 against 
companies that are found overcharging consumers.  
 
Besides price regulation, Government has also enabled access to affordable essential 
medicines through Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP), under which 
quality medicines are offered through Jan Aushadhi Kendras (JAKs) at rates that are typically 
50% to 80% lower than the prices of branded medicines.  In addition,  Under the Amrit 
(Affordable Medicines and Reliable Implants for Treatment) initiative of the Department of 
Health and Family Welfare, affordable medicines are provided for the treatment of cancer, 
cardiovascular and other diseases, implants, surgical dispo sables and other consumables etc., 
at an average discount of up to 50% on market rates through AMRIT Pharmacy stores set up 
in number of hospitals and healthcare institutions. Also, under the Free Drugs Service Initiati

CONSTITUTIONAL SAFEGUARDS OF UNDERTRIAL PRISONERS 
 
3275.  DR. GANAPATHY RAJKUMAR P:   
Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Supreme Court has proposed a nationwide mechanism for daily judicial 
access inside prisons and has proposed a policy exploring under which court -appointed 
judges visit jails everyday to ensure that undertrial prisoners are not deprived of 
constitutional safeguards when they are not produced before the courts; and 
(b) if so, the details thereof ? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF  
LAW AND JUSTICE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
 
(SHRI ARJUN RAM MEGHWAL) 
 
 
(a) & (b): The National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) constituted under Legal Services 
Authorities Act, 1987 , whose Patron-in-Chief is the Chief Justice of India, is providing free 
and competent legal services to all undertrial prisoners and other inmates across the country. 
NALSA has taken several steps for providing free legal services/ assistance to the undertrial 
prisoners by way of Legal Services Clinics and Prison Legal Aid Clinics (PLACs) . The 
Secretary, District Legal Services Authority (DLSA), and the Chairman, DLSA (District & 
Sessions Judge), undertake periodic prison visits under the NALSA Standard Operating 
Procedure on Access to Legal Aid Services to Prisoners and Functioning of the Prison Legal 
Aid Clinics, 2022 (SOP - 2022), to ensure effective legal aid delivery and institutional 
oversight of prisoners . As mandated by the SOP, the Secretary, DLSA visits and inspect s 
every PLAC at least once every month and ensures that all eligible undertrial prisoners are 
provided legal representation, monitors prison conditions, review s instances of non -
production of prisoners before courts  and take immediate steps to address the lapses. There 
are dedicated Undertrial Review Committ ees (UTRCs) constituted at the district level to 
examine instances where undertrial prisoners are not produced before the Remand or Trial 
Court, whether physically or through video -conferencing, due to logistical or other 
constraints, and to recommend appropriate remedial measures.
