सुदर्ध ए ां /अन्य सह यत  सेर् ए ां  उपिब्ध हैं और यदि नहीां, तो इसक े  क्य  क रण                   
हैं; और   
(घ) क्य  सरक र क  उि सांसिीय दनर् ाचन क्षेत्र में इन सुदर्ध ओां को सुदृढ़ करने तथ  
अदतररि सह यत  सेर् ओां को मांजूरी िेने क  प्रस्त र् है और यदि ह ां , तो तत्सांबांधी 
ब्यौर  क्य  है? 
 
उत् तर 
महिला एवं बाल हवकास राज्य मंत्री 
(श्रीमती साहवत्री ठाक ु र) 
 
(क) से (घ):  सरकार देश में महिलाओं की सुरक्षा, संरक्षा और सशिीकरण को सर्वोच्च 
प्राथहमकता देती िै। सरकार ने महिलाओं की शैहक्षक, सामाहिक, आहथिक और 
रािनैहतक सशिीकरण के हलए िीर्वन चक्र के सभी चरणों में उनकी आर्वश्यकताओं 

को पूरा करने िेतु बहुआयामी दृहिकोण अपनाया िै, ताहक र्वे तीव्र और सतत रािर ीय 
हर्वकास में समान भागीदार बन सक ें । यि 'महिला नेतृत्व र्वाला हर्वकास' 2047 तक 
‘हर्वकहसत भारत’ के लक्ष्य को प्राप्त करने के हलए आर्वश्यक िै। 
महिला एर्वं बाल हर्वकास मंत्रालय देश में महिलाओं और बच्चों के कल्याण के हलए क ें द्र 
प्रायोहित योिनाएां का कायािक्तन्वत कर रिा िै, हिन्हें तीन मुख्य र्दटाकि के अंतगित रखा 
गया िै अथाित: (1) महिलाओं की सुरक्षा, संरक्ष  और सशिीकरण के हलए हमशन शक्ति; 
(2) देश में पोषण एर्वं स्वास्थ्य संक े तकों में सुधार के हलए सक्षम आंगनर्वाडी एर्वं पोषण 
2.0; और (3) कहिन पररक्तिहतयों में बच्चों के संरक्षण एर्वं कल्याण के हलए हमशन 
र्वात्सल्य। 
‘दमशन शक्ति’ क  उद्देश्य मदहि ओां की सुरक्ष , सांरक्ष  और सशिीकरण क े  दिए दकए 
ज ने र् िे पहिोां को सुदृढ़ करन  है। दमशन शक्ति में मदहि ओां की सुरक्ष  और सांरक्ष  
तथ  सशिीकरण क े  दिए िो उप-योजन ए ाँ  क्रमशः  ‘सांबि’ और ‘स मर्थ्ा’ श दमि हैं। 
“सांबि” उप-योजन  मदहि ओां की सुरक्ष  और सांरक्ष  क े  दिए है। इसमें र्न स्टॉप सेंटर 
(ओएससी), मदहि  हेल्पि इन (डब्ल्यूएचएि), बेटी बच ओ बेटी पढ़ ओ (बीबीबीपी) और 
न री अि ित घटक श दमि हैं। 
1) वन स्टॉप सेंटर देश भर में हनिी और सार्वििहनक दोनों िानों पर हिंसा से पीहडत 
और संकटग्रस्त महिलाओं को एक ही स्थ न पर एकीक ृ त और तत्काल सहयोग और 
सिायता प्रदान करता िै। यि देश भर में िरूरतमंद महिलाओं को हचहकत्सा सिायता, 
कानूनी सिायता और सलाि, अिायी आश्रय, पुहलस सिायता और मनो-सामाहिक 
परामशि िैसी सेर्वाए ं प्रदान करता िै। र्वतिमान में, देश भर में 991 र्वन स्टॉप सेंटर 
क याशीि हकए गए िैं और इनकी िापना अथ ात 01 अप्रैि,2015 से 30 िून, 2026 
तक देश में 15.20 लाख से अहधक महिलाओं को सिायता प्रदान की गई िै। कन ाटक 
र ज्य में , बल्ल री सांसिीय दनर् ाचन क्षेत्र में बल्ल री दजिे में एक ओएससी और 
दर्जयनगर दजिे में िो ओएससी सदहत 44 र्न स्टॉप सेंटर क याशीि हैं तथ   कन ाटक 
र ज्य में इन ओएससी क े  म ध्यम से 44,926 से अदधक मदहि ओां को सह यत  प्रि न 
की गई है। चूाँदक यह योजन  म ांग-आध ररत है, इसदिए र ज्योां और सांघ र ज्य क्षेत्रोां को 
प्रत्येक दजिे में कम से कम एक ओएससी एर्ां दजन दजिोां में मदहि ओां क े  दर्रुद्ध 
अपर ध की िर अदधक है य  दजनक  भौगोदिक क्षेत्र बड  है र्ह ां तथ  आक ांक्षी दजिोां 
में अदतररि ओएससी स्थ दपत करने क े  दिए प्रोत्स दहत दकय  ज त  है।  
 
2) महिला िेल्पलाइन (डब्ल्यूएचएल-181) आपातकालीन और गैर-आपातकालीन 
दोनों क्तिहतयों में महिलाओं की सिायता के हलए 24 घंटे टोल-फ्री द ू रसंचार सेर्वाए ं 

प्रदान करती िै। यि हिंसा से प्रभाहर्वत महिलाओं को सिायता तथ  सरकारी योिनाओं 
और सेर्वाओं के बारे में िानकारी देती िै। इसकी स्थ पन  क े  ब ि से (1 अप्रैि, 2015 
से 30 जून, 2026 तक) पूरे िेश में मदहि  हेल्पि इनोां क े  म ध्यम से 1.04 करोड से 
अदधक मदहि ओां की सह यत  की गई है , दजसमें कन ाटक र ज्य में 1,23,643 
मदहि ओां की सह यत  की गई है। 
 
3) बेटी बचाओ बेटी पढाओ बाल हलंग अनुपात, बाहलका एर्वं महिला सशिीकरण से 
संबंहधत समस्य ओां के समाधान में सह यत  करती िै। इस योिना में हर्वहभन्न हितधारकों 
को सूहचत, प्रभाहर्वत, प्रेररत, श दमि करक े  और सशि बनाकर बाहलकाओं के प्रहत 
मानहसकता और व्यर्विार में पररर्वतिन लाने का प्रयास दकय  ज त  िै। बीबीबीपी सरकारी 
एिेंहसयों, मीहिया, नागररक समाि और बडे पैमाने पर िनता सहित हर्वहभन्न हितधारकों 
को एकजुट करक े  नीहतगत पिल से रािर ीय आंदोलन में बदल गई िै। 
 
4) अदालत योिना ग्राम पंचायत स्तर पर महिलाओं के हलए र्वैकक्तिक हशकायत हनर्वारण 
मंच प्रदान करती िै। इन अदालतों को घरेलू हिंसा और हलंग आधाररत अन्य हिंसा से 
संबंहधत छोटे म मिोां को पंचायत स्तर पर बातचीत, मध्यिता और आपसी सिमहत से 
सुलि के माध्यम से िल करने में सांकटग्रस्त महिलाओं की सिायता करने का दाहयत्व 
स ंपा गया िै ताहक उन्हें न्याय दमि सक े । 
 
“स मर्थ्ि” उप योिना महिलाओं के सशिीकरण के हलए िै। इसमें प्रधानमंत्री मातृ र्वंदना 
योिना (पीएमएमर्वीर्वाई), शक्ति सदन, सखी हनर्वास, पालना और संकि: महिला 
सशिीकरण क ें द्र (एचईिब्ल्यू) घटक शाहमल

entries.t: Working Women Hostels in Andhra Pradesh
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No.3277  
TO BE ANSWERED ON 07.08.2026  
   
WORKING WOMEN HOSTELS IN ANDHRA PRADESH  
  
3277. DR. GUMMA THANUJA RANI:  
               
        Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
  
(a)  whether Government has reviewed the adequacy of Working Women Hostel facilities 
(WWH) in view of increasing migration of women for education, employment and 
industrial work in Andhra Pradesh, if so, the details thereof;  
  
(b)  whether the Government has received any proposals from the said State for 
establishment/expansion of WWH outside Visakhapatnam district;  
  
(c)  if so, the details thereof along with the steps taken thereon; and  
  
(d)  the details of steps taken to ensure safety, affordability/accessibility of said hostels 
for working women?   
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF  WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR)  
   
  
(a) to (d)  Sakhi Niwas Scheme [Working Women Hostel (WWH)] under the overarching 
Mission Shakti, is a demand driven centrally sponsored scheme where States/UTs assess their 
requirement as per local needs and their proposals are approved by the Programme Ap proval 
Board (PAB) after discussion with States/UTs. The Scheme aims to promote availability of 
safe and conveniently located accommodation for working women and for those women who 
are pursuing higher education and training, with Day care facility for chi ldren in urban, semi -
urban and even rural areas where employment opportunity for women exists.   In this scheme, 
fund is provided for rental accommodation and component of construction  has been 
discontinued.  Funds under the Scheme are released to the State s/UTs in accordance with the 
guidelines of the Department of Expenditure through the Single Nodal Agency (SNA)/SNA -
SPARSH mechanism of the Public Financial Management System (PFMS).   
  

Presently, 23 Sakhi Niwas(WWH) are operational in the State of Andhra Pradesh.  The 
details of the operational Sakhi Niwas in the State of Andhra Pradesh are given at Annexure -I. 
  
           Further, under Part (X) – Construction of Working Women Hostels of the Special 
Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI) Scheme, an amount of ₹172.00 crore was 
allocated to the Government of Andhra Pradesh. The State Government submitt ed three 
proposals for the construction of Working Women Hostels in Visakhapatnam district, with a 
total project cost of ₹172.00 crore. These proposals were approved by the Department of 
Expenditure, and the first instalment of ₹113.52 crore was released t o the State Government 
during 2024–25. The details of the approved proposals are given at Annexure -II. 
  
To ensure the safety, affordability and accessibility of Working Women Hostels, 
secure accommodation is provided with boundary walls, security personnel, CCTV 
surveillance, biometric access/visitor registers, and adequate lighting, wherever applicable. 
Basic amenities such as furnished rooms, safe drinking water, sanitation, electricity, internet 
connectivity, and common facilities are also provided.   The Ministry also continuously 
monitors the implementation of the Scheme through physical and virtual review meetings with 
States/UTs, field visits by Ministry officials, and digital monitoring mechanisms. Based on the 
findings, appropriate measures are taken, and advisories are issued to States/UTs from time to 
time to facilitate effective implementation of th e Scheme.

 ANSWERED ON 07.08.2026 
  
SHIP REPAIR CLUSTERS 
  
3278. SHRI DHAIRYASHEEL SAMBHAJIRAO MANE: 
          SHRI SUDHEER GUPTA: 
          SHRI CHAVAN RAVINDRA VASANTRAO: 
       
  
Will the Minister of PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS be pleased to state: 
पȅन, पोत पįरवहन और जलमागŊ मंũी 
  
(a) the current status of the two proposed ship repair clusters at Kochi, Kerala and 
Vadinar, Gujarat, including the status of the DPR for the Vadinar cluster under review 
by the Government; 
  
(b) the current physical progress of the Pandu Ship Repair Facility, Assam and the 
connecting road project from Pandu Port to NH-27/NH-31; and 
  
(c) the current status and performance of the New Dry Dock and International Ship 
Repair Facility (ISRF) at CSL, Kochi, including the progress in onboarding an 
Operations & Maintenance partner? 
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS 
(SHRI SARBANANDA SONOWAL) 
 
(a):   International Ship Repair Facility (ISRF), Kochi of Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL) 
was inaugurated in January 2024 and repair of commercial and naval vessels are 
undertaken at this facility. The project of Vadinar Ship Repair Cluster has been 
approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) on May 05, 2026.  
(b): The current physical progress for ship repair facility at Pandu is 97%. The 
construction of alternative road from Pandu Port to NH-27 has been completed in 
March 2026. 
(c): The New Dry Dock (NDD) at CSL, Kochi, was inaugurated in January 2024. Since 
its operationalisation, shipbuilding of 05 vessels and ship repair of 02 vessels has 
been undertaken. 
  At the ISRF, repair of 45 vessels has been undertaken since its operationalisation 
in January 2024. 
  To strengthen the operational capabilities of the ship repair facilities, an enabling 
umbrella Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed between the CSL and 
Drydocks World (DDW) on 08.04.2025 to explore opportunities for collaboration in the 
development and operation of ship repair clusters, particularly at Kochi and Vadinar.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
  
LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.3279  
TO BE ANSWERED ON 07.08.2026  
  
CENTRAL ADOPTION RESOURCE AUTHORITY  
 
3279.  SHRI P P CHAUDHARY: 
SHRI P C MOHAN: 
SHRI BHOJRAJ NAG: 
SHRI VIJAY KUMAR DUBEY:  
SHRI MANISH JAISWAL: 
SHRI KOTA SRINIVASA POOJARY:  
SHRI ANURAG SINGH THAKUR:  
DR. HEMANT VISHNU SAVARA:  
SMT. ANITA NAGARSINGH CHOUHAN:  
DR. HEMANG JOSHI: 
SHRI NABA CHARAN MAJHI:  
SHRI NALIN SOREN: 
  
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
  
(a)    whether the Government has taken any new initiative through the Central Adoption 
Resource Authority (CARA) to make the adoption process, more transparent, simplified 
and timebound in the country;  
(b)    if so, the details thereof;  
(c)     the number of children adopted through CARA in the country during the last two years, 
along with the average waiting period for adoption, State/UT -wise including Rajasthan, 
Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka and Maharashtra;  
(d)    whether the Government proposes to increase the number of Specialised Adoption 
Agencies (SAAs)/strengthen the necessary facilities for the rehabilitation of abandoned 
and orphaned children in the country, if so, the details thereof along with the es timated 
timeline in this regard State/UT-wise and constituency -wise; 
(e)    the details of the measures taken to reduce the average time taken for completion of 
adoption process; and 
(f)     the details of the steps proposed to expand awareness and outreach services in the country? 
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR)  
  
(a) to (f):.  The Ministry of Women and Child Development is the nodal Ministry for the 
administration of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 (JJ Act, 2015), 
the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Model Rules, 2016 and the Adopt ion 
Regulations, 2022 for adoption through the Central Adoption Resource Authority (CARA). 
Under the JJ Act 2015, the Child Welfare Committees (CWCs) have been empowered to take 

decisions with regard to the children in need of care and protection including orphaned, 
abandoned and surrendered.  
  
The District Magistrate has been empowered to issue Adoption Orders as per Section 58(3) 
and Section 61 of the JJ Act, 2015 read with Regulation 36 of Adoption Regulations, 2022. 
As per Schedule XIV of the Adoption Regulations 2022, timelines have been defined for each 
stakeholder.  
  
The waiting period of the Prospective Adoptive Parents (PAPs) depends on the availability of 
children who are declared legally free for adoption by CWC. It also depends on the choice of 
the PAPs to adopt from the age group preferred.  
  
In order to reduce delays and to maintain transparency, CARA has digitized end -to-end 
process through the digital platform of Adoption Module under Mission Vatsalya portal  and 
regular monitoring and follow -ups is done with the State Governments and UT 
Administrations including all stakeholders to expedite the process, as per the Schedule XIV 
of the Adoption Regulation, 2022 which has stipulated timeline for authorities and agencies 
working in adoption. 
  
The Ministry is implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme namely ‘Mission Vatsalya’ in 
all States and Union Territories on predefined cost sharing basis between the Central and the 
State Governments to deliver various services for children in difficult circumstances including 
orphan children. The scheme provides institutional care and non-institutional care. Child Care 
Institutions (CCIs) established under the Mission Vatsalya scheme provide, inter -alia, age -
appropriate education, access to vocational train ing, recreation, health care, counselling etc. 
The Scheme also supports the Specialized Adoption Agencies (SAAs) registered under the 
Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act,2015, where adoptable children of 
below six years of age are provid ed residential care.  
  
States and UTs have been advised to establish at least one Specialised Adoption Agency 
(SAA) in each district in accordance with Sections 65 and 66 of the JJ Act, 2015, read with 
Adoption Regulations, 2022 (Regulations 3 & 5). 795 SAAs have been approved u nder 
Mission Vatsalya Scheme for all State Governments and Union Territory Administrations as 
on 29.07.2026. All SAAs are mandatorily onboarded onto the integrated CARINGS -Mission 
Vatsalya system, enabling end -to-end digital processing of adoption cases in cluding referral, 
matching, and documentation. Compliance is monitored through real -time dashboards at 
Central and State levels, and through periodic review meetings.  
  
The nationwide Information, Education and Communication (IEC) activities as well as 
localized outreach programmes to promote adoption and foster care are conducted under 
Mission Vatsalya. CARA also undertakes awareness and outreach

suburban railways, thereby saving travel time and money for the general public;  
  
(c) the details of the policy of the Union Government to ensure that the ticket fares 
remain affordable for ordinary citizens;  
  
(d) the specific financial provisions made to empower the traditional business of 
the local Koli community and fishermen through modern jetties without causing any 
disruption to their livelihoods; and  
  
(e) the current status of projects undertaken to expand Ro-Ro (Roll-on/Roll-off) 
and passenger ferry services in Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh? 
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS 
(SHRI SARBANANDA SONOWAL) 
  
(a): On account of non-availability of fiscal space in the current Sagarmala scheme, 
no new project for construction of jetties and passenger terminals along the eastern 
and western coasts of Mumbai has been sanctioned in the current financial year.  

  
(b): Under the current Sagarmala Scheme, 18 Ro-Ro / Ro-Pax infrastructure 
projects worth ₹ 561 crore have been sanctioned in the state of Maharashtra to 
improve coastal connectivity. Development of water transport infrastructure, including 
passenger jetties, ferry terminals and Ro-Ro/Ro-Pax facilities, promotes coastal 
shipping and inland water transport as sustainable and efficient modes of transport. 
These projects provide an alternative mode of passenger and vehicular movement, 
thereby reducing pressure on congested roads and suburban rail networks, reducing 
travel time, fuel consumption and logistics costs, while contributing to environmental 
sustainability. 
  
(c): The Central Government provides financial assistance under Sagarmala 
scheme for development of water transport infrastructure. As per the notification 
no.12/2017- Central Tax (Rate) dated 28.06.2017, transportation of passengers, with 
or without accompanied belongings, by public transport, other than predominantly for 
tourism purpose, in a vessel between places located in India is exempted from GST. 
The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) has also exempted port & 
vessel related charges for the Ro-Pax and passenger ferry operations till 22.01.2027. 
  
(d): Government of Maharashtra has informed that the Department of Fisheries is 
undertaking the development of modern fishing jetties and allied infrastructure to 
strengthen the traditional livelihoods of the Koli community and fishermen. The details 
of financial assistance provided by MoPSW under the Sagarmala scheme for fishing 
harbours / fish landing centres in the state of Maharashtra is available at Annexure 1. 
  
(e): Under Sagarmala Scheme, in the state of Maharashtra 18 Ro-Ro / Ro-Pax 
infrastructure projects worth ₹ 561 crore have been sanctioned to improve coastal 
connectivity. Out of these, 13 projects worth ₹ 340 crore are completed in the state of 
Maharashtra. The details are available at Annexure 2. No Ro-Ro/Ro-Pax/ferry projects 
have been sanctioned in the state of Madhya Pradesh under Sagarmala scheme.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3282 
ANSWERED ON 07.08.2026 
  
DAMAGE TO EMBANKMENTS IN SUNDERBANS DUE TO CARGO SHIP 
MOVEMENT 
 
3282. SHRI BAPI HALDAR: 
 
       Will the Minister of PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS be pleased to state: 
पƣन, पोत पǐरवहन और जलमाग[ मंğी 
 
(a)  whether the Government is aware that the frequent movement of large cargo 
vessels through the inland waterways of the Sundarbans delta is causing severe 
erosion and damage to riverbank embankments in districts such as South 24 
Parganas, including the Mathurapur region; 
(b) whether any study has been undertaken to assess the ecological and structural 
impact of heavy ship traffic on small islands such as Mousuni, Ghoramara, Kumirmari, 
Satjelia, Chhotomollakhali and Amtoli that are facing existential threats due to 
embankment breaches, saline water ingress and wave pressure; 
(c)   if so, the details thereof and the corrective steps taken by the Government in this 
regard; and 
(d) whether the Government is considering either limiting or regulating the cargo 
movement through ecologically fragile zones or allocating special funds under 
Sagarmala or any other scheme for long-term protection and fortification of 
embankments, if so, the details thereof?  
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS 
(SHRI SARBANANDA SONOWAL) 
  
 (a)       Riverbank erosion is a complex natural phenomenon influenced by several 
factors, including river morphology, sediment transport, hydrological regime, tidal 
action, bank material and local hydraulic conditions. Inland Waterways Authority of 
India (IWAI), an autonomous organization under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and 
Waterways (MoPSW) undertakes only navigational interventions for maintenance of 
fairways in only 30-45 meter channel of the river and no specific evidence has been 
established indicating that movement of shallow-draft Inland Water Transport (IWT) 

vessels operating on National Waterway (NW)-97 (Sundarbans Waterways) has 
caused riverbank or embankment erosion. Fairway maintenance activities are planned 
keeping in view navigational requirements and applicable environmental safeguards.   
  
(b) & (c)  No dedicated study has been undertaken by IWAI and Govt. of West Bengal 
to establish a direct correlation between IWT operations and riverbank erosion in NW-
97. However, IWAI carries out periodic hydrographic surveys and continuous 
monitoring of channel conditions for maintenance of navigable fairways. The 
hydrographic data, together with river behaviour and navigational requirements, forms 
the basis for planning and implementation of fairway maintenance measures. 
  
(d)  IWAI regulates the movement of vessels through ecologically fragile zones with 
following measures:  
 Restricting  speed of the vessels within the sanctuary. 
 Fitting vessels with propeller guards and dolphin deflectors. 
 Restricting navigation to designated channels. 
 Using non-toxic anti-fouling paints. 
MoPSW has not allocated  special funds under Sagarmala or any other scheme for 
long-term protection and fortification of embankments.

3287.  Dr. Alok Kumar Suman: 
                
Will the Minister of Chemicals and Fertilizers be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has made any assessment regarding the availability 
of fertilizers to farmers across the country, if so, the details of production, allocation 
and distribution of major fertilizers during the last three years, State-wise and year-
wise; 
 
(b) whether any shortage of fertilizers has been reported, if so, the details thereof 
along with the corrective measures taken thereon; 
 
(c) the details of subsidies provided on fertilizers during the said period;

encourage alternative nutrient sources; and

farmers? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS 
 
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
 
(a) to (e) Following steps are taken by the Government every season for ensuring 
timely and adequate availability of fertilizers in the country: 
 
(i) Before the commencement of each cropping season, Department of Agriculture 
and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with all the State Governments, 
assesses the State-wise & month-wise requirement of fertilizers. On the basis of 
requirement projected by DA&FW, Department of Fertilizers (DoF) allocates 
adequate quantities of fertilizers to States by issuing monthly supply plan and 
continuously monitors the availability. 
 
(ii) The movement of all major subsidized fertilizers is monitored throughout the 
country by an on-line web-based monitoring system called integrated Fertilizer 
Management System (iFMS). 
 

(iii) The gap between demand (requirement) and production for Urea & other 
fertilizers is met through imports. The import for the season is also finalized well 
in advance to ensure timely availability.  
 
(iv) The State Governments are regularly advised to coordinate with manufacturers 
and importers for streamlining the supplies through timely placement of indents. 
 
(v) Regular coordination is done with the Ministry of Railways for giving sufficient 
rakes, priority to fertilizers and for timely evacuation of rakes for States. 
 
(vi) The distribution of fertilizers within the State at district/block level is done by the 
concerned State government. 
 
In view of above, the availability of fertilizers viz. Urea, DAP, MOP and NPKS has

Distribution of Fertilizers in Karnataka 
 
3289. Shri P C Mohan: 
 
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Bharat brand fertilizers under the One Nation One Fertilizer initiative are 
being distributed in Karnataka and if so, the details thereof along with the quantity of 
Bharat Urea, Bharat DAP, Bharat MOP and Bharat NPK supplied to the said State 
during the last two years, year-wise; 
 
(b) the number of fertilizer companies, State Trading Entities and Fertiliser Marketing 
Entities distributing fertilisers under the Bharat brand in the said State; 
 
(c) whether the criss-cross movement of fertilizers has reduced in the said State, if 
so, the details thereof along with the benefits accrued to farmers; and 
 
(d) whether the current availability position of fertilizers in the said State is sufficient 
to meet the requirement for Kharif season 2026, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS 
 
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
 
(a) to (d) One Nation One Fertilizer scheme stands implemented under 
"Pradhanmantri Bhartiya Janurvarak Pariyojna" (PMBJP) with effect from 24th 
August, 2022. All fertilizers companies viz Public sector, Cooperative and Private 
sector are required to sell subsidized fertilizers under brand name "BHARAT" across 
the country. The objective of the scheme is to increase the availability basket of 
fertilizers; take care of dilemma among farmers in choosing from plethora of brands 
manufactured by various companies available in the markets, reduce the crisscross 
movement and further ensure timely supply of fertilizers across the country, including 
the State of Karnataka. By consolidating branding under a single "BHARAT" brand, 
the scheme fosters transparency, combats malpractices, and ensures equitable 
access to essential nutrients for crops. 
Before the commencement of each cropping season, Department of Agriculture and 
Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with all the State Governments, assesses 

 
the State-wise & month-wise requirement of fertilizers. On the basis of requirement 
projected by DA&FW, Department of Fertilizers (DoF) allocates adequate quantities of 
fertilizers to States by issuing monthly supply plan and continuously monitors the 
availability. 
Accordingly, the available of fertilizers, viz. Urea, DAP, MOP and NPKS has remained 
adequate in the State of Karnataka during the last two years and ongoing Kharif 2026 
season. The information regarding the requirement, availability and sales of said 
fertilizers in the State during the last two years is placed at Annexure-A and ongoing 
season is placed at Annexure-B. 
Moreover, the major fertilizer suppliers/companies operating in the State of 
Karnataka are GSFC, IFFCO, KRIBHCO, MFL, PPL, RCF, RFCL, SPIC, FACT, IPL, 
CIL, GFL, STL, NBCL and NFL.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
DEPARTMENTOF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 3293
TO BE ANSWERED ON 07TH AUGUST, 2026
WORKING OF DOCTORS BEYOND WORKING HOURS
†3293. SHRI AJENDRA SINGH LODHI:
Will the Minister of HEALTHAND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has sought a compliance report
from the Ministry of Health regarding the issue of postgraduate resident doctors being made
to work beyond the prescribed limits and the violation of the Postgraduate Medical Education
Regulations, 2023 at R.G. Kar Medical College, Kolkata;
(b) if so, the details thereof along with the action taken so far against the concerned officials
and the institution in the said matter and the details of the person held responsible for not
submitting the compliance report on time;
(c) whether resident doctors in various medical colleges are being made to work up to 80-100
hours per week which is a violation of the prescribed norms across the country, if so, the
details thereof, State/UT-wise; and
(d) whether the Government is ensuring strict compliance with the safety and working-hour
limits for resident doctors and if so, the details thereof?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SMT. ANUPRIYAPATEL)
(a) to (d): Case No 441/90/0/2025 of National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) was
referred to Ministry to submit the action taken report on a complaint dated 17.03.2025.
Matter was examined in the Ministry in consultation with National Medical Commission
(NMC) and submitted the report to NHRC, wherein it was informed as follows:
i. As per regulation 5.2 (ii) of the PGMER, 2023, "All post-graduate students will work
as full time resident doctors. They will work for reasonable working hours and will be
provided reasonable time for rest in a day”. Further, as per Regulation 9.1 of the
PGMER, 2023, "For non- compliance or omission, the PGMEB will penalize the
medical college/ institutions.". PGMEB, NMC is empowered to take action against

the concerned medical college/ institution, as per specified under Regulation 9.2 of
the PGMER, 2023.
ii. NMC Anti-Ragging Committee convened a meeting on 14.08.2024 to deliberate upon
the incident and its wider implications for the safety, well-being, and working
conditions of medical students and resident doctors across the country. As an
immediate measure, NMC issued an Advisory dated 13.08.2024 to all Medical
Colleges and Institutions.
iii. MoHFW/DGHS has issued directions to all Central Government Hospitals/Institutes,
AIIMSs and all Medical Colleges to ensure filing of institutional FIR within
maximum period of 6 hours of any incident of violence against doctors and other
healthcare personnel vide OM dated 16.08.2024 and also issued advisories to
States/UTs vide D.O. letters dated 23.08.2024 and 03.09.2024 to take immediate
measures for enhancing security and providing safer working environment for
medical professionals.
iv. The incident at R.G. Kar Medical College, West Bengal was taken up by the Hon’ble
Supreme Court of India in SMW (Crl) No. 2 of 2024, wherein the Hon'ble Court had
constituted a National Task Force (NTF) to formulate recommendations for redressal
of the issues regarding safety, well-being and working conditions of medical
professionals. The Report of NTF had been submitted to the Hon'ble Court in
November, 2024.
Also, as "Public Health and Hospitals" is a state subject, the respective State
Governments/UT Administrations prescribe norms for doctors' working hours, service
conditions, duty rosters in the concerned institutions, taking into account local requirements
and applicable service rules.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
  
LOK SABHA

ANSWERED ON 07.08.2026  
  
SAFETY AND SECURITY OF WOMEN THROUGH THE NIRBHAYA FUND  
  
3294. SHRI BUNTY VIVEK SAHU  
  
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  be pleased to state: 
  
(a)  whether the Govemment  has taken effective measures for the safety and security of 
women through the Nirbhaya Fund, if so, the details thereof, including the benefits 
accrued to the State of Madhya Pradesh, particularly in Chhindwara district;  
(b)  whether the Govemment is considering the expansion of One Stop Centres, women's 
support services and other safety infrastructure to strengthen the safety and security of 
women in Chhindwara the said district, if so, the details thereof;  
(c)  whether the Govemment is implementation any special campaigns to further strengthen 
safety awareness and provide prompt assistance mechanisms for women and girls in 
rural and tribal areas, if so, the details thereof; and  
(d)  whether the Govemment is implementing any special action plan to ensure the effective 
and expeditious utilisation of the Nirbhaya Fund in the said State, if so, the details 
thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR)  
   
(a) to (d): Aimed at enhancing the safety and security of women and girls in the country, 
Nirbhaya Fund has been set up as a dedicated non -lapsable corpus fund administered by the 
Department of Economic Affairs(DEA),Ministry of Finance in accordance with the framework 
and guidelines issued by the Government from time to time. The Institutional mechanism 
envisages a co -ordinated approach involving the concerned Central Ministries, State 
Governments and Implementing Agencies fo r conceptualization, execution and monitoring of 
the projects. Projects are conceptualized, planned and brought to the Inter - Ministerial 
Empowered Committee( EC) for appraisal and recommendation. Upon appraisal and 
recommendation of the proposals by the EC, the sponsoring Ministry’s   respective Competent 
Financial Authority (CFA)   gives the financial approval, after which the allocation of funds 
from the Nirbhaya Fund is made in the Budget of the sponsoring Ministry/ Department by the 
Ministry of Finance from the Nirbhaya Fund. The projects/ schemes under Nirbhaya Fund are 
demand driven and generally have staggered implementati on schedules and the responsibility 

of implementation of the project lies with the concerned sponsoring Ministries/Departments/ 
State Governments.  
The Inter Ministrerial  Empowered Committee also reviews the status of implementation of 
projects, and expenditure on approved projects from time to time in conjunction with the 
concerned sponsoring Ministries/ Departments/ State Governments/ UTs. The concerned 
Ministries / Depa rtments / State Governments/ UTs also monitor the progress of 
implementation at their own levels.  
Under the Nirbhaya Fund, upto the financial year 2025-26, a total amount of Rs. 320.71 Crore 
has been released/utilized for projects implemented through different implementing agencies 
in the State of Madhya Pradesh including the projects of Ministry of Women and Child 
Development viz. OSCs and WHL. 
One Stop Centre (OSC) provides integrated and immediate support and assistance under one 
roof to women affected by violence and those in distress, both in private and public spaces all 
across the country. It provides services like medical aid, legal aid an d advice, temporary 
shelter, police assistance and psycho -social counselling to needy women across the country. 
As on date, 991 One Stop Centres have been made operational across the country and since 
inception, i.e. 1st April, 2015 to 30th June, 2026, ove r 15.20 lakh women have been assisted 
through One Stop Centres across the country. As on date, 63 OSCs are operational in Madhya 
Pradesh which have assisted over 1,65,475 women; out of which one OSC in Chhindwara is 
operational which has assisted 1095 women.  
Women Helpline (WHL -181) provides 24 -hour toll -free telecommunication services to 
support women in both emergency and non -emergency situations. It offers assistance to 
women affected by violence and provides information about government schemes and 
services. Since inception (1st April, 2015 to 30th June, 2026), over 1.04 crore women have 
been assisted through Women Helplines across the country. In the State of Madhya Pradesh, 
WHL has assisted over 3,83,834 women till 30th June, 2026.  
To strengthen convergence and ensure seamless access to support services, OSCs have been 
integrated with the Women Helpline (WHL), and so far, 661 OSCs have been integrated. 
Through this integration, women can be referred to appropriate services in a timel y and 
coordinated manner. Further, the Women Helpline has also been integrated with the 
Emergency Response Support System (ERSS -112), Child Helpl

HEALTHY DIETS FOR CHILDREN  
 
3296. THIRU D M KATHIR ANAND:  
 Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
(a)  the details of the focus accorded to enhancing nutritional security for children through 
improved access to balanced diets, micronutrient -rich foods, protein supplementation 
and nutrition education under Government programmes;  
  
(b)  the details of the approach adopted for encouraging informed dietary choices among 
parents, caregivers and educational institutions by promoting awareness of healthy 
eating habits, quality food ingredients and age -appropriate nutrition for children; 
  
(c)  the details of the support extended for strengthening nutrition interventions through the 
Integrated Child Development Services, Poshan Abhiyaan/related schemes to States 
and Union Territories; 
  
(d)  the details of the collaboration with healthcare professionals, nutrition experts, 
educational institutions and food industry stakeholders for promoting scientific 
nutrition awareness; and 
  
(e)  the details of the measures being proposed for improving the availability, 
affordability/accessibility of nutritious foods to ensure better growth, health and 
cognitive development among children?  
  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR)  
  
(a) to (e):     Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 (Mission Poshan 2.0)  has 
provisioned Supplementary Nutrition to all beneficiaries including Children (6 months to 6 
years), Pregnant Women, Lactating Mothers and Adolescent Girls (14-18 years). It is provided 
in the form of Take -Home Ration (THR), Morning Snacks and Hot Cooked Meal (HCM). 

Supplementary Nutrition is provided to the beneficiaries in accordance with the nutrition norms 
contained in Schedule -II of the National Food Security Act, 2013, revised in January 2023. 
The old norms were largely calorie -specific; however, the revised norms are more 
comprehensive and balanced in terms of both quantity and quality based on the principles of 
diet diversity that provides for quality protein, healthy fats and micronutrients ( Calcium, Zinc, 
Iron, Dietary Folate, Vitamin A, Vitamin -B6 and Vitamin B -12). Additional Nutrition is also 
provided to Severely Acute Malnourished (SAM) children (6 months to 5 years) in the form of 
THR. 
The Ministry has recently issued the Comprehensive Guidelines for Supplementary Nutrition 
which emphasize on improving the quality, diversity and acceptability of Supplementary 
Nutrition, adherence to prescribed nutritional norms and quality standards. Gui delines also 
focus on nutrition and health education for caregivers, promoting the use and benefits of THR 
including counselling on age -appropriate complementary feeding practices and to conduct 
targeted awareness programmes focusing on reducing consumptio n of edible oils, salt and 
sugars in daily diets in line with the Dietary Guidelines for Indians, 2024, released by the Indian 
Council of Medical Research – National Institute of Nutrition (ICMR -NIN). States and UTs 
are also advised to consult nutrition ex perts and technical institutes, like ICMR -NIN, 
Agricultural Universities, Home Science Colleges, etc., for formulating State -specific recipes 
for supplementary nutrition based on local palate/tastes using locally available foods.  
To improve acceptability and consumption of Supplementary Nutrition, States and UTs have 
been given full flexibility to design menus and recipes based on local food habits, cultural 
preferences and availability of indigenous ingredients. Supplementary nutr ition incorporates 
locally available cereals, millets, pulses, vegetables, nuts and other nutrient-rich foods, thereby 
promoting dietary diversity while ensuring greater acceptance among beneficiaries.  
One of the major activities undertaken under Mission Poshan 2.0 is Community Mobilization 
and Awareness Advocacy to educate people on nutritional aspects as adoption of good nutrition 
habit requires sustained efforts for behavioural change. State and UTs a re conducting and 
reporting regular sensitisation activities under Jan Andolans during Poshan Maah and Poshan 
Pakhwada, celebrated in the months of September and March -April, respectively. More than 
150 crore Jan Andolan activities have been conducted since 2018 through 16 Jan Andolans, 
each helped sensitizing not only the target beneficiaries but communities at large.  
Community Based Events (CBEs) have served as a significant strategy in changing nutritional 
practices and all Anganwadi workers (AWWs) are required to conduct two Community Based 
Events every month.  So far, around 10.5 crore CBEs have been reported on Poshan Tracker 
from April 2022 to June 2026.

(a) to (c): A third-party evaluation and impact assessment of Poshan Abhiyaan was conducted 
by NITI Aayog in 2020 and it found the relevance of Poshan Abhiyaan to be satisfactory for 
tackling malnutrition in the country.    
In 2021, the World Bank conducted a survey under Poshan Abhiyaan across 11 States including 
Andhra Pradesh. The States were selected based on high prevalence of stunting among children 
and anaemia among women. The findings of the survey demonstrated improv ed nutrition 
behaviors with respect to the services delivered through the Poshan Abhiyaan. The survey also 
found that the program's nutrition messages reached more than 80% of women, and that 81% 
of women practiced exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months.  
An outcome-based evaluation study of Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 (Mission 
Poshan 2.0)  was conducted again by Development Monitoring and Evaluation 
Office (DMEO), NITI Aayog in 2025 in 12 States (including Andhra Pradesh) and one Union 
Territory. Evidence indicated that in its current form, Mission Poshan 2.0 represents the 
Government’s latest effort to holistically combat malnutrition and promote child development, 

by building on past programs with a converged and strengthened approach. High uptake and 
utilisation of Anganwadi services, such as supplementary nutrition, growth monitoring, and 
counselling, serves as a strong indicator that Poshan Abhiyaan has been frui tful in driving 
awareness and encouraging behavioural change among beneficiaries.  
Ministry of Women and Child Development (MoWCD ) under Mission Poshan 2.0, has rolled 
out ‘Poshan Tracker’ digital application as an ICT based governance tool for monitoring and 
reviewing of services being provided to beneficiaries. The application has enabled the Ministry 
as well as States & UTs to re view the implementation of the scheme on various parameters 
including health and nutrition status of the women and children and to make course corrections. 
For last mile tracking of Service Delivery, Facial Recognition System (FRS) in Poshan Tracker 
Application has been introduced for distribution of Take -Home Ration and to ensure that 
benefit is given only to the intended beneficiary registered in the application. Such Aadhaar 
based tracking has enabled proper identification of beneficiaries, prevention of  leakages and 
eliminating ghost entries.

3302. SHRI SUNIL BOSE:
Will the Minister of HEALTHAND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government is aware of the Global Tuberculosis Report 2024, which states that
India had the highest tuberculosis burden in the year 2023 contributing to 26 per cent of global TB
deaths, if so, the details thereof;
(b) the details of the allocation of funds for TB elimination in the country during each of the last
five years, year-wise and State/UT-wise;
(c) the initiatives taken by the Government to address the issue of multi drug-resistant TB in the
country; and
(d) whether the Government has been successful in the implementation of the National Strategic
Plan for Tuberculosis to eliminate TB by 2025, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons
therefor?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL)
(a) to (d) The Government has implemented National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP)
under the aegis of National Health Mission (NHM). As per World Health Organisation’s
Global TB report 2024, it was estimated that India contributed to 26% of total TB deaths
globally in 2023, however as per Global TB Report 2025, the proportion reduced to 25%
in 2024.
With the implementation of the National Strategic Plan for TB, as per the World Health
Organization’s Global TB Report 2025 the country’s estimated TB incidence (per lakh
population) has declined by 21% from 237 in year 2015 to 187 in year 2024, almost twice the
global decline (12%). Estimated TB mortality (per lakh population) declined by 25% from 28
in year 2015 to 21 in year 2024. The treatment coverage increased from 53% in 2015 to 92%
in 2024, which led to reduction in missing cases from 15 lakhs to less than 1 lakh.
Measures taken by the Government to address multi drug-resistant TB across the country are
as under:
 Early detection through intensified screening in OPD/IPD and community based active
case finding campaign with focus on vulnerable population and congregate settings
 Provision of free drugs and diagnostics to TB patients including for drug-resistant TB

 Universal Drug Susceptibility Testing (UDST) for all TB patients to detect drug-resistant
TB through 11,296 Nucleic Acid Amplification Test (NAAT) laboratories at district & sub
-district levels
 Established a network of 108 Line Probe Assay, 74 Liquid Culture Testing Laboratories,
37 Intermediate Reference Laboratories and 6 National Reference Laboratories for
diagnosis of drug resistance and quality assurance
 For decentralized treatment, 815 Drug Resistant TB treatment centres are established
 Introduction of shorter, safer, all oral drug-resistant TB treatment regimen, which includes
BPaLM regimen (Bedaquiline, Pretomanid, Linezolid and Moxifloxacin) for management
of drug- resistant TB cases
 Intensified Information, Education & Communication (IEC) campaigns to reduce stigma,
enhance community awareness and improve health seeking behaviour
 Track & monitor notified TB cases through Ni-kshay portal
Under NHM, funds for NTEP are provided as part of RCH Flexipool to all State/UTs. Further,
the details of allocation of funds for TB elimination in the country during last five years, year-
wise and State/UT-wise, is placed as Annexure.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS 
DEPARTMENT OF FERTILIZERS 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3303 TO BE ANSWERED ON: 07.08.2026 
 
 
Establishment of Fertilizer Manufacturing Units in Amritsar 
 
3303. Shri Gurjeet Singh Aujla: 
 
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Union Government is considering to support fertilizer unit in Amritsar to 
reduce import dependency, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) whether it is true that such a unit would not only reduce transportation costs and import 
dependency, but also generate massive employment opportunities for local youth, support 
agriculture and reduce the burden of excessive subsidy by enabling cheaper domestic 
production, if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(c) whether the proposal of such units under the schemes promoting self-reliance in agri- 
inputs and prioritise border areas like Amritsar for such strategic investment, if so, the details 
thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS 
 
 (SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
 
(a) to (c): With regard to Urea, the Government had announced New Investment Policy (NIP) 
– 2012 on 2nd January, 2013 and its amendment on 7th October, 2014 to facilitate fresh 
investment in the urea sector and to make India self-sufficient in the urea sector. Total 6 new 
urea units have been set up under NIP-2012 which includes 4 urea units set up through Joint 
Venture Companies (JVC) of nominated PSUs and 2 urea units set up by the private 
companies. The units set up through JVC are Ramagundam urea unit of Ramagundam 
Fertilizers and Chemicals Ltd (RFCL) in Telangana and 3 urea units namely Gorakhpur, 
Sindri and Barauni of Hindustan Urvarak & Rasayan Limited (HURL) in Uttar Pradesh, 
Jharkhand and Bihar, respectively. The units set up by private companies are Panagarh urea 
unit of Matix Fertilizers and Chemicals Ltd. (Matix) in West Bengal; and Gadepan-III urea 
unit of Chambal Fertilizers and Chemicals Ltd. (CFCL) in Rajasthan. Each of these units has 
installed capacity of 12.7 Lakh Metric Tonne per annum (LMTPA). These units are highly 
energy efficient as they are based on latest technology. Therefore, these units have together 
added urea production capacity of 76.2 LMTPA, thereby total indigenous urea production 
capacity (Reassessed Capacity, RAC) has increased from 207.54 LMTPA during 2014-15 to 
269.42 LMTPA during 2026-27. Further, an exclusive policy for the revival of Talcher unit of

a new Greenfield Urea plant of 12.7 LMTPA at coal gasification route has also been 
approved. Also, setting up of a new Brownfield Ammonia-Urea Complex named as Assam 
Valley Fertilizer and Chemical Company Ltd. (AVFCCL) with an annual capacity of 12.7 Lakh 
Metric Tonne of Urea through Joint Venture within the existing premises of Brahmaputra 
Valley Fertilizer Corporation Limited (BVFCL), Assam has been approved. These two 
projects are under execution phase. 
 
Also, the Government notified the New Urea Policy (NUP) – 2015 on 25th May, 2015 for 
the existing 25 gas-based urea units with one of the objectives of maximizing indigenous 
urea production beyond RAC.  The NUP-2015 has led to additional production of urea by 
20-25 LMT as compared to the production during 2014-15 annually.  
 
Above steps together have facilitated increase of Urea production from level of 225 LMT 
per annum during 2014-15 to a record Urea Production at 314.07 LMT during 2023-24. 
During 2025-26, 293.30 LMT of Urea was produced in the country. 
 
In addition to this, on 15.07.2026, CCEA approved National Investment Policy for Urea-
2026 for Aatmanirbhar Bharat (NIPU-2026) for making fresh investments in Urea Sector.

entries.head:
1 
 
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LAW AND JUSTICE 
DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE 
                                                            
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3307 
TO BE ANSWERED ON FRIDAY, THE 07th AUGUST, 2026 
 
SANCTIONED STRENGTH OF JUDGES IN HIGH COURTS 
 
3307. PROF. SOUGATA RAY: 
           
Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of the growing pendency of cases in various High 
Courts despite periodic increase in the sanctioned strength of Judges, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government proposes to substantially increase the sanctioned strength of 
Judges in all High Courts, on the lines of the recent increase in the sanctioned strength of Judges 
of the Supreme Court;  
(c) if so, the details thereof including the proposed increase and the timeline for 
implementation, High Court-wise; 
(d) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of the additional number of Judges 
required in each High Court based on pendency, institution and disposal of cases, judge -to-
population ratio and regional requirements, if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the measures being taken by the Government in consultation with the judiciary to ensure 
timely filling of vacancies, strengthening of judicial infrastructure and reduction of pendency 
in the High Courts? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF LAW  
AND JUSTICE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
 
(SHRI ARJUN RAM MEGHWAL) 
 
(a) to ( e): The Judges of the High Courts are appointed under Article 217 and 224 of the 
Constitution of India and according to the procedure laid down in the Memorandum of 
Procedure (MoP) prepared in 1998 pursuant to the Supreme Court Judgment of October 6, 
1993 (Second Judges case) read with their Advisory Opinion of October 28, 1998 (Third Judges 
case).  
 

2 
 
As per the Memorandum of Procedure (MoP), the responsibility for initiation of 
proposals for appointment of Judges in the Supreme Court vests with the Chief Justice of India, 
while the responsibility for initiation of proposals for appointment of Judges in the High Courts 
vests with the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court, in consultation with two senior-most 
puisne Judges of the High Court. As per the MoP, the High Courts are required to make 
recommendations at least 06 months before the occurrence o f a vacancy. However, this time 
limit is rarely observed. For appointments to the High Courts, the views of concerned State 
Government are obtained in accordance with the MoP. The recommendations also have to be 
considered in the light of such other reports as may be available to the Government in respect 
of the names under consideration. The recommendations of the High Court Collegium, the 
State Governments and the Government of India are then forwarded to the Supreme Court 
Collegium (SCC) for advice. Appo intment of Judges in the higher judiciary is a continuous, 
integrated and collaborative process between the executive and the judiciary. It requires 
consultation and approval from various Constitutional Authorities both at State and Central 
level. Only those persons whose names have been recommended by the SCC are appointed as 
Judges of the High Courts.  
 
 The Judge strength of the High Courts is increased from time to time. The strength of 
High Courts has increased from 906 in 2014 to 1122 Judges in 2026. 
 
Disposal of cases pending in various courts lies within the domain of the judiciary . 
Timely disposal of cases in courts depends on several factors which, inter -alia, include 
availability of adequate number of judges and judicial officers, supporting court staff and 
physical infrastructure, complexity of facts involved, nature of evidence, co-operation of stake 
holders viz. bar, investigation agencies, witnesses and litigants. However, the Government is 
fully committed for speedy disposal of cases and reducing pendency. The Government has 
taken several initiatives to provide an ecosystem for  faster disposal of cases by the judiciary 
which, inter-alia, includes amalgamation of latest technologies for increasing access to justice 
and greater transparency under the e -Courts Mission Mode Project, better infrastructure for 
courts, increase in strength of subordinate judiciary, policy and legislative measures in the areas 
prone to excessive litigation,  enactment of New Criminal Laws, promoting Alternate Dispute 
Resolution mechanism and emphasis on human resource development. 
 
 
***

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
DEPARTMENT OF FERTILIZERS

The recent geopolitical tensions disrupted global supply chains for fertilizers and 
raw materials, resulting in higher freight and insurance costs, shipment delays, and price 
volatility. However, fertilizer availability in the country remained largely adequate through 
diversified sourcing and Government interventions. Government has undertaken measures to 
diversify import sources by exploring procurement opportunities from various countries. 
Moreover, the fertilizer industry has also collectively procured fertilizers and raw materials 
through an industry consortium to ensure transparent price discovery, improve bargaining 
power with global suppliers, and secure timely availability of fertilizers and raw materials. The 
budgetary allocation for fertilizer subsidy is reviewed periodically, based on which, the process 
for seeking additional budgetary allocation, on requirement, is undertaken, as per the extant 
provision. 
 
The following Steps are taken by the Government every season for ensuring timely and 
adequate supply of fertilizers across the States/UTs, including the State of Kerala: 
I. Before the commencement of each cropping season, Department of Agriculture and Farmers 
Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with all the State Governments, assesses the State-wise & 
month-wise requirement of fertilizers. On the basis of requirement projected by DA&FW, 
Department of Fertilizers (DoF) allocates adequate quantities of fertilizers to States by issuing 
monthly supply plan and continuously monitors the availability. 
II. The movement of all major subsidized fertilizers is monitored throughout the country by an 
online web-based monitoring system called integrated Fertilizer Management System (iFMS). 
III. The gap between demand (requirement) and production for Urea & other fertilizer is met 
through imports. The import for the season is also finalized well in advance to ensure timely 
availability.  
IV. The State Governments are regularly advised to coordinate with manufacturers and 
importers for streamlining the supplies through timely placement of indents.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
 
LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3309  
TO BE ANSWERED ON 07.08.2026  
  
NUTRITIONAL STATUS OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN  
3309. SHRI ZIA UR REHMAN: 
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether the Government has assessed the nutritional status of children and pregnant 
women under POSHAN Abhiyaan, if so, the details thereof;  
(b)  the details of malnutrition cases reported during the last three years, State -wise; and 
(c)  the details of the corrective measures being taken to improve nutrition and strengthen 
Anganwadi services? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR)  
  
(a) to (c):  Under the Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 (Mission Poshan 2.0), 
the ‘Poshan Tracker’ digital application has been rolled out by Ministry of Women and Child 
Development (MoWCD ) as an ICT based governance tool for continuous monitoring and 
tracking of all services being provided to the beneficiaries registered at Anganwadi Centres 
(AWCs). Technology under Poshan Tracker is being leveraged for dynamic identification of 
stunting, wasting, under -weight prevalence among children under 5 years of age group. The 
State-wise and year -wise information on nutrition indicators among children under 5 years is 
available at Poshan Tracker dashboard: https://www.poshantracker.in/statistics.  
Various measures have been taken by the MoWCD to improve nutritional outcomes and 
strengthen Anganwadi services:  
• Under Mission Poshan 2.0, two lakh Anganwadi Centres (AWCs) located in 
Government buildings have been approved to be upgraded as Saksham Anganwadis for 
delivery of improved nutrition and for ECCE activities. These Saksham Anganwadis  
are equipped with better infrastructure such as LED screens, water filtration system, 
Poshan Vatika, Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) material and Building as 
Learning Aid (BaLA) paintings. 
  

• Supplementary Nutrition in the form of Hot cooked meal (HCM) and Take -Home 
Ration (THR) is provided to Children (6 months to 6 years), Pregnant Women, 
Lactating Mothers and Adolescent Girls in accordance with the nutrition norms 
contained in Schedule-II of the National Food Security Act, 2013. Additional Nutrition 
is also provided to Severely Acute Malnourished (SAM) children in form of Take -
Home Ration (THR). 
• MoWCD and Ministry of Health & Family Welfare have jointly released the Protocol 
for Management of Malnutrition in Children to prevent and treat severely acute 
malnutrition in children and for reducing associated morbidity and mortality.  
• Mission Poshan 2.0 empowers the frontline functionaries by providing them with 
smartphones along with data recharge facility. Further, there is a provision of Growth 
Monitoring Devices (GMDs) as Infantometer, Stadiometer, Weighing Scale-Infant and 
Weighing Scale -Mother & Child at each Anganwadi Centre (AWC) for the regular 
growth monitoring of registered beneficiaries.  
• Anganwadi Workers (AWWs) conduct structured home visits to support pregnant 
women, lactating mothers, and young children (0 -3 years) through nutrition 
counselling, caregiving guidance, and promotion of early childhood development.  
• One of the major activities undertaken is Community Mobilization and Awareness 
Advocacy in the form of Jan Andolans (Poshan Maah and Poshan Pakhwada celebrated 
in the months of September and March -April respectively) to educate people on 
nutritional aspects as adoption of good nutrition habit requires sustained efforts for 
behavioural change. 
• Poshan Vatikas are set up under Mission Poshan 2.0 at Anganwadi Centers across the 
country to encourage consumption of local and seasonal fruits, vegetables, thereby 
improving diet-diversity and increase the intake of micronutrients.

 3310. SHRI TANUJ PUNIA: 
 
        Will the Minister of PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS be pleased to state:

(a) the names of the Ministers and Embassies with whom coordination 
mechanisms have been established for rapid medical response and emergency 
evacuation under the Seafarer First Plan; 
(b) whether the Government has made it mandatory for shipowners and 
recruitment agencies not to force any Indian seafarer to undertake duty on sensitive 
routes without adequate protection; and 
(c) the role of dedicated liaison officers to be appointed to assist the families of 
affected sailors?  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS 
(SHRI SARBANANDA SONOWAL) 
  
(a) The Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways is coordinating through Ministry of 
External Affairs and Indian Embassies all over the world and also  through Directorate 
General of Maritime Administration (DGMA) a subordinate body under this Ministry 
with Port State Authorities, Flag State Authorities and Recruitment and Placement 
Service License [RPSL] agencies, for rapid medical response and emergency 
evacuation under the seafarer First Plan.  
(b)  The Directorate General of Maritime Administration (DGMA), has issued a 
series of advisories in view of the maritime security environment, in conflict-affected 
regions, including the Persian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz, Black Sea, and the Yemen/Red 
Sea region. These advisories are precautionary in nature and are intended to enhance 
the safety and security of Indian seafarers. The details are placed at Annexure. 
(c)  The Government, through the Directorate General of Maritime Administration 
(DGMA), has designated dedicated officers for continuous coordination, 
communication, and welfare support to Indian seafarers and their families during 
maritime emergencies and crisis situations. These officers function as liaison officers 
and are responsible for maintaining regular engagement with the Next of Kin (NoK), 

Recruitment and Placement Service Licence (RPSL) agencies, shipping companies, 
Indian Missions abroad, maritime administrations, and other concerned stakeholders 
to ensure timely assistance and coordinated response. Vide Order dated 02.03.2026, 
a dedicated 24×7 Quick Response Team has been constituted in DGMA to provide 
immediate response, evacuation coordination, crisis management, and welfare 
support. The responsibilities assigned to the designated officers include: 
 Maintaining continuous communication with the families and Next of Kin (NoK) 
of affected seafarers. 
 Coordinating with RPSL agencies, shipping companies, Indian Missions 
abroad, port authorities, and other stakeholders for obtaining real-time 
information and facilitating timely assistance. 
 Providing immediate support through the DG Communication Centre operating 
round-the-clock via dedicated telephone, WhatsApp, and email channels. 
 Facilitating evacuation, repatriation, welfare assistance, and dissemination of 
advisories issued by the Directorate General of Maritime Administration and the 
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways. 
 Monitoring the status and location of affected seafarers, submitting periodic 
situation reports, and ensuring prompt response to emergencies affecting the 
safety, security, and welfare of Indian seafarers.  
Accordingly, a structured mechanism has been established through designated liaison 
officers and a dedicated 24×7 response team to ensure continuous engagement with 
affected families and timely coordination for all welfare, relief, communication, and 
support-related matters.

Excessive Use of Fertilizers 
 
3312.  Dr. Prabha Mallikarjun: 
 
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has made any assessment regarding nitrate contamination 
of groundwater, pesticide residues and environmental impacts associated with 
excessive fertilizer usage, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether any studies has been conducted regarding the impact of fertilizer and 
agrochemical use on human health, water quality and ecosystem sustainability during 
the last five years, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government has identified regions affected by groundwater contamination 
and soil degradation linked to agricultural chemical use, if so, the details thereof; 
(d) the measures being taken to promote sustainable fertilizer practices, nano-fertilizers, 
bio-fertilizers and environmentally responsible nutrient management; and 
(e) whether any groundwater quality monitoring, soil restoration/sustainable agriculture 
initiatives have been implemented in Karnataka, particularly in Davanagere district, if 
so, the details thereof, district-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
 (SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
 
(a) to (c)   The Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) informed that they generate 
groundwater quality data at the regional scale through its groundwater quality monitoring 
programme and various scientific studies. Groundwater quality is monitored across the 
country through the Ground Water Quality Monitoring Stations, and the analyzed data are 
published in the Annual Ground Water Quality Reports of CGWB. As per the Annual 
Ground Water Quality Report–2025, 20.71% of groundwater samples analyzed were found 
to contain nitrate above the permissible limit of 45 mg/L (BIS IS 10500). Nitrate 
contamination above the permissible limit has been observed in parts of 502 districts 
across 26 States/UTs. The State/UT-wise details are placed at Annexure-I. Further, 
CGWB informed that they have not conducted any specific studies on pesticide residues, 

environmental impacts of excessive fertilizer usage, health impacts of fertilizer/ 
agrochemical use, or soil degradation specifically linked to agricultural chemical use. 
Department of Agriculture, Government of Karnataka informed that they have not 
conducted any exclusive study on nitrate contamination of groundwater, pesticide residues 
and environmental impacts associated with excessive fertilizer usage. However, balanced 
application of NPK fertilizers in conjunction with organic manure (FYM/bio-fertilizers) to 
maintain soil health, organic carbon content and crop productivity is being promoted. 
Imbalanced and excessive use of nitrogenous fertilizers (especially Urea) leads to soil 
acidity/alkalinity, secondary and micronutrient deficiencies (such as Zinc and Boron) and 
secondary leaching of nitrates into shallow aquifers. Further, ICAR and the Directorate of 
Plant Protection, Quarantine & Storage (DPPQ&S) under the Monitoring of Pesticide 
Residues at National Level (MPRNL) scheme regularly analyse the  samples of  food 
commodities and surface water sources. Pesticide residue levels exceeding Maximum 
Residue Limits (MRL) remain under control. Under the MPRNL project and the State Sector 
Program, samples of fruits, vegetables, grains, fish/marine products, herbs, and water are 
drawn to test for pesticide residues. If samples are found to contain residues exceeding 
the Maximum Residue Limit (MRL) or traces of off-label pesticide usage, farmers in the 
concerned areas are sensitized about the ill effects of excessive and off-label chemical 
applications. 
Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) informed that long-term studies 
conducted by them have shown that imbalanced nutrient application, particularly sole 
application of nitrogen, leads to decline in crop yield and soil health. Excess nitrogen is 
primarily lost through nitrate leaching, resulting in groundwater nitrate contamination, with 
Nitrate concentrations exceeding the permissible limit of 10 mg/L in some areas. Studies 
also showed that groundwater nitrate levels increase with fertilizer application rates, with 
higher contamination observed in high fertilizer-use areas.

3314. SHRI ESWARASAMYK:
Will the MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government is aware of the rising incidence of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus
(GDM) among pregnant women in India as indicated by recent clinical studies and
national health surveys, if so, the details thereof;
(b) the prevalence data on GDM reported during the last five years, year-wise and State-wise;
(c) whether the Government has taken note of the significant variation between NFHS survey
findings and hospital-based clinical estimates indicating possible under-diagnosis of
GDM in the country, if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the steps taken by the Government under the National Health Mission (NHM),
RMNCH+A framework and other maternal health programmes to ensure universal
screening, early diagnosis and effective management of GDM at the primary healthcare
level?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SMT. ANUPRIYAPATEL)
(a) to (c) The details of the ICMR-INDIAB National Study (ICMR-INDIAB-24)
conducted on Prevalence of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus in India is available in the
following link:
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12744553/
(d) Under National Health Mission (NHM), the Government of India has taken various
initiatives/steps to ensure universal screening, early diagnosis and effective management
of GDM at the primary healthcare level, which placed as below;
 The Government of India has released Guidelines on Diagnosis and Management of
Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM) in pregnant women in 2014 and revised Guidelines
in 2018.
 Financial assistance is provided to States/UTs for ensuring the availability of logistics
for GDM screening and for capacity-building of frontline healthcare providers, including

Medical Officers, Staff Nurses, Community Health Officers (CHOs), Auxiliary Nurse
Midwives (ANMs), and Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHAs).
 Universal screening for Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM) through the Oral
Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT) has been incorporated into the essential antenatal care
(ANC) package for all pregnant women.
 Pregnant women identified as GDM are tracked till 45th day of delivery under
Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA/Extended-PMSMA). Further,
incentives are provided to ASHA and High Risk Pregnant (HRP) women for 3 additional
follow-ups visit.
 Implementation and progress of GDM screening are monitored through supportive
field visits and periodic National and State level review meetings.
 Universal GDM screening is promoted through regular Information, Education and
Communication (IEC) and Behaviour Change Communication (BCC) activities to
enhance awareness and encourage early detection and timely management.

MANUFACTURING OF AYUSH DRUGS 
 
3316. SHRI NA VEEN JINDAL 
Will the Minister of AYUSH be pleased to state: - 
(a) the total number of complaints received by the Government regarding false, misleading or 
unfounded advertisements issued by AYUSH drug manufacturers during each of the last three 
years; 
(b) the action taken against the erring companies in this regard; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to strengthen the regulatory/advisory framework to 
curb such advertisements; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (IC) OF THE MINISTRY OF AYUSH 
 
(SHRI PRATAPRAO JADHA V) 
(a) & (b) The Ministry of Ayush has been implementing the Pharmacovigilance Programme for 
Ayush drugs since 2018 to monitor the safety of Ayush medicines through surveillance, 
reporting and assessment of suspected adverse drug reactions, thereby promoting their safe and 
rational use. The Programme also monitors misleading advertisements relating to Ayush drugs 
to curb false and exaggerated claims and safeguard consumer interests. The Programme was 
incorporated under the Ayush Oushadhi Gunavatta Evam Uttpadan Samvardh an Yojana 
(AOGUSY) in 2021. The total number of complaints received by the Ministry regarding 
misleading advertisements related to Ayush drugs under Pharmacovigilance Program for Ayush 
drugs in last three years are attached at Annexure-1.  
Further, Ministry of Ayush has launched an IT enabled online portal “Ayush Suraksha” to track 
the reported Misleading Advertisements (MLAs)/Objectionable Advertisements (OAs) and 
Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs) in 2025.  As per information received from State/UTs, the 
misleading advertisements reported on Ayush Suraksha Portal since its inception and action 
taken thereon are attached at Annexure-2. 
(c) & (d) As per the section 8 of Drugs & Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) 
Act, 1954, States and UTs are empowered to notify officers to enforce the provisions of Drugs 

& Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954  and Rules there under . It 
encompasses the provisions for prohibition of misleading advertisements and exaggerated 
claims of drugs and medicinal substances including Ayush medicines, which appear in the print 
and electronic media and Ministry of Ayush has issued advisories and gives direction to SLAs 
to enforce and regulate as per the provision of this Act. 
 
Further, the f ollowing actions have been taken by the Ministry to strengthen the 
regulatory/advisory framework to curb misleading/objectionable advertisements- 
 
i. Pharmacovigilance Program for Ayush drugs under  Ayush Oushadhi Gunavatta evam 
Uttpadan Samvardhan Yojana (AOGUSY) is working through a three -tier network of a 
National Pharmacovigilance Centre (NPvCC), Five Intermediary Pharmacovigilance 
Centres (IPvCs) and 97 Peripheral Pharmacovigilance Centres (PPvCs) established across 
the country. To enhance public awareness regarding Ayush medicines and its objectionable 
advertisements, a total of 4,165 awareness programmes for Ayush professionals and Public 
have been conducted, benefiting 3,71,477 participants by Pharmacovigilance centres. 
ii. Ministry of Ayush has launched an IT enabled online portal “Ayush Suraksha” to track the 
reported Misleading Advertisements (MLAs)/Objectionable Advertisements (OAs) and

MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
  
LOK SABHA 
UN-STARRED QUESTION No. 3317  
TO BE ANSWERED ON 07.08.2026  
  
SAMBAL AND SAMARTHYA COMPONENTS UNDER MISSION SHAKTI  
3317. SHRI MALAIYARASAN D:  
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state : 
(a)  the current status of implementation of Mission Shakti, including the projects/services 
operational under its Sambal and Samarthya components in Tamil Nadu;  
(b)  the details of funds allocated, released and utilised for implementation of the said Mission 
in the said State during the last five years;  
(c)  the number of beneficiaries provided assistance through One Stop Centres, Women 
Helpline services and other women empowerment initiatives under the said Mission, 
district-wise including Kallakurichi Parliamentary Constituency;  
(d)  whether the Government has assessed the challenges faced in implementation of said 
Mission, including availability of trained personnel, infrastructure gaps and awareness 
among women, particularly in rural and remote areas of the State; and  
(e)  if so, the details of the steps being taken by the Government to enhance access to 
protection, rehabilitation, skill development and livelihood opportunities for women 
through this Mission in the said State?  
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR)  
  
(a) To (e) The Ministry of Women and Child Development is implementing Centrally 
Sponsored Schemes in the country for the welfare of women and children, which are placed 
under three verticals, viz. (1) Mission Shakti, for safety, protection and empowerment  of 
women; (2) Saksham Anganwadi & Poshan 2.0 for improving nutrition & health indicators in 
the country; and (3) Mission Vatsalya, for protection and welfare of children in difficult 
circumstances.  

The ‘Mission Shakti’ aims at strengthening interventions for women safety, security and 
empowerment. Mission Shakti comprises of two verticals ‘Sambal’ for safety and security of 
women and ‘Samarthya’ for empowerment of women.  
The ‘Sambal’ has components of One Stop Centre (OSC), Women Helpline (WHL), Beti 
Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) and Nari Adalat.  
1. One Stop Centre (OSC)  provides integrated and immediate support and assistance 
under one roof to women affected by violence and those in distress, both in private and 
public spaces all across the country. It provides services like medical aid, legal aid and 
advice, temporary s helter, police assistance and psycho -social counselling to needy 
women across the country. As on date, 991 One Stop Centres have been made 
operational across the country and since inception, i.e. 1st April, 2015 to 30th June, 
2026, over 15.20 lakh women ha ve been assisted through One Stop Centres across the 
country. As on date, 59 OSCs are operational in the State of Tamil Nadu; out of which 
one OSC is operational in Kallakurichi district and two OSCs are operational in Salem 
district, which have assisted o ver 1,82,957 women. 
2. Women Helpline (WHL -181) provides 24 -hour toll-free telecommunication services 
to support women in both emergency and non-emergency situations. It offers assistance 
to women affected by violence and provides information about government schemes 
and services. Since inception (1st April, 2015 to 30th June, 2026), over 1.04 crore 
women have been assisted through Women Helplines across the country. In the State 
of Tamil Nadu, WHL has assisted over 2,59,509 women till 30th June, 2026.  
3. Beti Bachao Beti Padhao  helps to address Child Sex Ratio (CSR) and related issues 
of empowerment of girls and women. The scheme tries to create mindset and 
behavioural changes towards the girl child by informing, influencing, motivating, 
engaging, and empowering various stakehol ders. BBBP has transformed from a policy 
initiative into a national movement by mobilizing various stakeholders, including 
government agencies, media, civil society, and the public at large.  As per latest reports 
of Health Management Information System (HM IS) of Ministry of Health & Family 
welfare (MoHFW), the Sex Ratio at Birth (SRB) is showing improving trends and has 
increased from 918 to 929 at national level during 2014-15 to 2025-26 (provisional). In 
the State of Tamil Nadu, the Sex Ratio at Birth (SRB) has increased from 917 to 937 
during 2014-15 to 2025-26 (provisional).

schools at secondary level has increased from 75.51% in 2014-15 to 83.4% in 2025-26.

level has increased from 93.82% in 2014 -15 to 99.6% in 2025-26.
