STRENGTHENING OF PRIMARY HEALTH SERVICES IN REMOTE AREAS
†3318. SHRI CHINTAMANI MAHARAJ:
Will the Minister of HEALTHAND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether there has been a significant increase in the number of beneficiaries, treatments
and hospital admissions under the Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana
(AB-PMJAY) in Chhattisgarh, including Surguja district and if so, the details thereof;
(b) whether special steps have been taken by the Union Government to strengthen primary
healthcare services, screening, diagnostic services and health insurance coverage through
Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (AAMs) in tribal and remote regions of the State, such as
Surguja District and if so, the details thereof;
(c) the progress made under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) and other digital
health initiatives to expand and integrate digital health services across various health schemes;
and
(d) the major achievements of the scheme towards improving the availability of healthcare
services, reducing out-of-pocket health expenditure for beneficiaries and achieving Universal
Health Coverage (UHC) in tribal and rural areas of the country?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND
FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) There has been a significant increase in the utilization of Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan
Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) in Chhattisgarh, including Surguja district. The
number of Ayushman Cards created in the State increased from 3.18 lakh in FY 2018–19 to
14.52 lakh in FY 2025–26, while authorised hospital admissions increased from 3.42 lakh to
15.22 lakh during the same period, reflecting the growing outreach and utilization of the
Scheme by eligible beneficiaries.
As on 31.07.2026, a total of 2.47 crore Ayushman Cards have been created in the State,
including 8.49 lakh Ayushman Cards in Surguja district. Further, a total of 93.17 lakh hospital
admissions have been authorized in Chhattisgarh, of which 2.93 lakh hospital admissions
have been authorized in Surguja district.

(b): Under National Health Mission, through 1.86 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (AAM) in
the country, (including 5898 in Chhattisgarh State and 218 in Sarguja district),
comprehensive primary healthcare is provided by strengthening Sub Health Centres and
Primary Health Centres. These AAM provide preventive, promotive, rehabilitative and
curative care for an expanded range of services encompassing reproductive and child
healthcare services, communicable diseases, non-communicable diseases and other health
issues.
(c): The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) was launched by the Government of
India in September 2021 to support the development of an integrated, citizen-centric national
digital health ecosystem. Several national health programme platforms, including
AB-PMJAY ,Nikshay, Reproductive and Child Health and Non-Communicable Disease are
integrated with ABDM. In addition, various government and private Hospital Management
Information System have also been integrated with ABDM, enabling these systems to create
Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA), create & share digital health records for
seamless interoperability across the ecosystem. The progress of ABDM, as on 31.07.2026 for
the country is as under:
 ABHA created for citizens – 95.99 crore
 Health Record Linked to citizen’s ABHA – 107.55 crore
 Verified Healthcare Professionals on Healthcare Professional Registry – 10.33 lacs
 Verified Health Facilities on Health Facility Registry- 5.40 lacs
 Facilities using ABDM-enabled software – 2.76 lacs
(d): AB-PMJAY has significantly improved access to quality secondary and tertiary
healthcare services for eligible beneficiaries through a nationwide network of empanelled
public and private hospitals. As on 31.07.2026, a total of 38,374 hospitals have been
empanelled under the scheme, across the country.
Further, more than 12.69 crore hospital admissions, amounting to more than Rs. 1.92 lakh
crore, have been authorized under the scheme, enabling eligible beneficiaries to avail
cashless treatment under the scheme.

SOCIAL DIVERSITY AND REPRESENTATION IN HIGHER JUDICIARY 
 
†3321. SHRI MURARI LAL MEENA: 
           
Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the relatively disproportionate representation of 
various social categories, regions and women in the appointment of judges to the High Courts 
and the Supreme Court, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government has consolidated data regarding the social category, gender and 
regional representation of judges in the High Courts and the Supreme Court, if so, the details 
thereof; 
(c) whether the Government has conducted any study or consultation regarding the 
enhancement of the participation of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward 
Classes, women and Economically Weaker Sections in the higher judiciary, if so, the key 
findings thereof; and 
(d) the policy steps being taken by the Government to promote transparency, equal opportunity 
and broader social representation in the higher judiciary? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY 
OF LAW AND JUSTICE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
 
(SHRI ARJUN RAM MEGHWAL) 
 
(a) to (d): Appointment of Judges to the Supreme Court and High Courts is made under Articles 
124, 217 and 224 of the Constitution of India, which do not provide for reservation for any 
caste or class of persons. Therefore, category-wise data pertaining to representation of any caste 
or class of persons among the Judges of Supreme Court and the High Courts is not centrally 
available.  
 
As per the Memorandum of Procedure (MoP), the responsibility for initiation of 
proposals for appointment of Judges in the Supreme Court vests with the Chief Justice of India, 
while the responsibility for initiation of proposals for appointment of Judges in  High Courts 

2 
 
vests with the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court. However, the Government is 
committed to enhancing social diversity in judiciary and has been requesting the Chief Justices 
of High Courts that while sending proposals for appointment of Judges, due consideration be 
given to suitable candidates belonging to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward 
Classes, Minorities and Women to ensure social diversity in the appointment of Judges in High 
Courts. Only those persons who are recommended by th e Supreme Court Collegium, are 
appointed as Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts.

(a) to (e) Following steps are taken by the Government every season for ensuring 
timely and adequate availability of fertilizers in the country, including the State of Uttar 
Pradesh: 
 
(i) Before the commencement of each cropping season, Department of Agriculture 
and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with all the State Governments, 
assesses the State-wise & month-wise requirement of fertilizers. On the basis of 
requirement projected by DA&FW, Department of Fertilizers (DoF) allocates 

adequate quantities of fertilizers to States by issuing monthly supply plan and 
continuously monitors the availability. 
 
(ii) The movement of all major subsidized fertilizers is monitored throughout the 
country by an on-line web-based monitoring system called integrated Fertilizer 
Management System (iFMS). 
 
(iii) The gap between demand (requirement) and production for Urea & other 
fertilizers is met through imports. The import for the season is also finalized well 
in advance to ensure timely availability.  
 
(iv) The State Governments are regularly advised to coordinate with manufacturers 
and importers for streamlining the supplies through timely placement of indents. 
 
(v) Regular coordination is done with the Ministry of Railways for giving sufficient 
rakes, priority to fertilizers and for timely evacuation of rakes for States. 
 
(vi) The distribution of fertilizers within the State at district/block level is done by the 
concerned State government.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.  3323 
ANSWERED ON 07.08.2026  
  
CHILD CARE INSTITUTIONS  
 
3323.  SHRI K RADHAKRISHNAN:  
  
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
  
(a)  the number of registered Child Care Institutions functioning in the country, State-wise; 
(b)  whether the Government has conducted inspections of these institutions during the last 
three years, if so, the details of any violations detected therein;  
(c)  the details of the action taken against institutions found violating the provisions of the 
Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015; and  
(d)  the details of the measures being taken to strengthen monitoring and ensure the safety, 
rehabilitation and welfare of children residing in such institutions  
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR)  
 
  
(a) to (d) :  The Ministry of Women and Child Development is the nodal Ministry for the 
administration of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 (JJ Act, 2015) 
which is the primary legislation for ensuring safety, security, dignity and well -being of 
children and is implemented by all the States and Union Territories. The Act creates statutory 
structures at the State and District levels which include State Child Protection Society, Child 
Welfare Committees, Juvenile Justice Boards, District Child Protection Units. It also provides 
for establishment of Child Care Institutions (CCIs).  
  
Under the JJ Act 2015, the Child Welfare Committees (CWCs) have been empowered to take 
decisions with regard to the children in need of care and protection including orphaned, 
abandoned and surrendered children. They are also mandated to monitor the functi oning of 
the Child Care Institutions (CCIs). Similarly, the Juvenile Justice Boards (JJBs) are 
empowered to take decisions regarding the welfare of children in conflict with law. The Act 
defines standards of care and protection to secure the best interest of children living in CCIs 
and aims to provide family environment through non -institutional care services which 
includes sponsorship, foster care and aftercare.  
  
This Ministry is implementing Centrally Sponsored Scheme namely ‘Mission Vatsalya’ 
through the State Governments and Union Territory Administrations on pre -defined cost 
sharing basis between the Centre and the State Governments to deliver various services for 

children in difficult circumstances, which include both institutional and non -institutional care 
services.  
  
Under Section 54 of the JJ Act, 2015, the State Governments and UT Administrations appoint 
Inspection Committees to assess the basic facilities and infrastructure of the Institutions for 
maintaining their standards. Also, Sections 32 to 34 of JJ Act, 2015 mention the procedure for 
mandatory reporting including offence for non -reporting and penalty.  
  
The JJ Act, 2015 and Rules made thereunder provide for inspection of Child Care Institutions 
by State Level Inspection Committee and District Level Inspection Committee. The District 
Level Inspection Committee is constituted by the District Magistrate with  Additional District 
Magistrate as Chairperson. The District Level Inspection Committee inspects all CCIs in the 
district and submits the report of the findings to the District Magistrate or the State 
Government for improvement and development of CCIs in a ccordance with the provisions of 
the JJ Act, 2015 and Rules made thereunder. The District Magistrate being the focal point in 
the district for implementation of the Act, takes follow up action on the report of inspection 
committees and ensure that correcti ve measures are taken in a time bound manner.  
  
The Ministry of Women and Child Development has developed an integrated unified Mission 
Vatsalya Portal in consultation and coordination with States and UTs.  The TrackChild portal 
for Missing/Found Children, and Khoya -Paya application for Missing/Sighted C hildren have 
been integrated with this unified Mission Vatsalya Portal. The TrackChild  module of the 
Mission Vatsalya portal is implemented with support and involvement of various stakeholders

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AYUSH 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3324 
ANSWERED ON 07/08/2026 
KERALA AS GLOBAL HUB FOR AYURVEDA TOURISM 
 
3324. SHRI SHAFI PARAMBIL 
 
Will the Minister of AYUSH be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any special initiatives to promote Kerala as a 
global hub for Ayurveda and wellness tourism during the last five years; 
(b) if so, the details of the funds allocated and released to Kerala, scheme-wise; 
(c) the details of the research projects, Centres of Excellence, medicinal plant cultivation 
programmes and AYUSH institutions supported by the Central Government in the State; and 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to promote evidence -based Ayurveda, international 
accreditation and exports of Ayurvedic products from Kerala? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (IC) OF THE MINISTRY OF AYUSH 
 
(SHRI PRATAPRAO JADHAV) 
(a) & (b)  The Government has adopted a comprehensive strategy to promote Ayush -based 
tourism in the country. Ministry of Tourism has formulated a National Strategy and Roadmap 
for Medical and Wellness Tourism in consultation with other Ministries including Ministry of 
Ayush. 
To facilitate international visitors seeking Ayush -based treatments, the Government 
introduced a separate category of Ayush Visa on 27 July 2023. Ministry of Ayush has also 
signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with India Tourism Development 
Corporation (ITDC), Ministry of Tourism to work together for the promotion of Medical 
Value Travel (MVT) in Ayurveda and other traditional systems of medicine.  So far, Ministry 
of Ayush has org anized two Medical Value Travel Summits, one for Western zone on 
30.09.2024 at Mumbai with participation of States/UTs of Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan, 
Goa, and Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu, and the other for the Southern Zone on 
26.05.2025 at Chennai with participation of States/UTs like Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, 
Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Puducherry, with the aim of strengthening India’s position 
in Medical Value Travel. 
 
(c)  The research activities in the State are undertaken through the units/institutes under the 
respective Research Councils of the Ministry of Ayush. At present, 34 research programmes 
are being carried out at the National Homoeopathy Research Institute in Mental Health 

2 
 
(NHRIMH), Kottayam, which functions under the Central Council for Research in 
Homoeopathy (CCRH). Two institutes under the Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic 
Sciences (CCRAS) are functioning in the State of Kerala, namely the National Ayurveda 
Research Institute for Panchakarma (NARIP), Cheruthuruthy, and the Regional Ayurveda 
Research Institute (RARI), Thiruvananthapuram. CCRAS has undertaken various research 
projects in the State, including Medico -Ethno Botanical Surveys (MEBS), ethno -dietary 
studies, inventory of phytodiversity of medicinal plants, and programmes related to the 
cultivation of medicinal plants. The Clinical Research Unit of the Central Council for 
Research in Unani Medicine (CCRUM) is functioning at Edathala, Kerala, and provides 
healthcare services across geriatric, reproductive, and non-communicable disease sectors. The 
Siddha Regional Research Institute (SRRI) functioning under the Central Council for 
Research in Siddha (CCRS), situated in Poojapura, Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala is dedicated 
exclusively to research in Siddha medicine. The institute is actively involved in scientific 
validation of traditional Siddha formulations, evidence -based clinical studies, and 
standardization of Siddha medicines.  This institute engages in Intramural Research (IMR) 
projects on clinical research, Drug Standardization Research and Medicinal Plants Research. 
 Under the National A yush Mission (NAM), the Government of India extends 
financial assistance to the State of Kerala for strengthening Ayush healthcare services 
through the State Annual Action Plans (SAAPs), which are approved annually in accordance 
with the provisions of the NAM Operational Guidelines. The support provided under NAM 
includes both recurring and non -recurring grants. Recurring grants cover the supply of 
medicines and contingencies to Ayush institutions, as well as human resource support for 
Ayush hospitals. Non -recurring grants include infrastructure development such as 
construction, renovation, upgradation and strengthening of Ayush healthcare facilities, along 
with the provision of equipment and furniture for Ayush institutions. 
 Under the ‘Conservation, Development and Sustainable Managem ent of Medicinal 
Plants’ a Central Sector Scheme implemented by National Medicinal Plants Board (NMPB), 
Ministry of A yush, project based financial support is provided for research activities on 
various aspects of medicinal plants to government as well as private universities/research 
institutions/organizations across the country. The details are at Annexure I.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF AYUSH

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3325    
ANSWERED ON 07/08/2026 
 
ADOPTION OF AYUSH GRID IN NABARANGPUR, ODISHA 
 
3325. Shri Balabhadra Majhi  
 
Will the Minister of AYUSH be pleased to state:  
(a) the details of the progress made in the implementation of various digital platforms and e -
Governance tools, including the AYUSH Grid and My AYUSH Integrated Services Portal, 
and their implementation in the Nabarangpur Parliamentary Constituency of Odisha; 
 
(b) the extent to which the AYUSH Grid has been adopted by States, Union Territories and  
health institutions and its impact on healthcare delivery in the Nabarangpur Parliamentary  
Constituency of Odisha; and 
 
(c) the details of the Government's roadmap for the further digital transformation of the  
AYUSH Grid and its integration with national health programmes, including the measures  
proposed for the Nabarangpur Parliamentary Constituency, Odisha? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (IC) OF THE MINISTRY OF AYUSH  
 
(SHRI PRATAPRAO JADHAV)  
 
(a) The Ayush Grid  project serves as the IT backbone of the Ayush sector, driving digital 
transformation across healthcare, research & development, Ayush drug administration, 
medicinal plants, education & awareness, capacity building and global/media outreach.   
Under this initiative, twenty -four e -governance platforms have been developed and made 
accessible across the country. The My Ayush Integrated Services Portal (MAISP), the master 
portal of the Ministry of Ayush  available at https://www.maisp.ayush.gov.in , integrates all 
Ayush-related applications and services into a unified digital ecosystem. An AI -enabled 
chatbot (Beta version) has also been deployed to assist visitors and enhance user experience. 
The portal facilitates citizen-centric access to various services and schemes and enables real -
time monitoring and data-driven decision-making. (Details available at: maisp.ayush.gov.in)  
Similarly, the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) -compliant Ayush Hospital 
Management Information System (AHMIS) has been deployed to digitize healthcare delivery 

and improve the management of Ayush health facilities. The Ayush Anudan Portal has 
streamlined the submission, processing, approval, and monitoring of funding proposals under 
various Central Sector Schemes of the Ministry. The Ayush Research Portal serves as a 
centralized digital repository of over 43,000 curated Ayush research publications, facilitating 
easy access for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers. The Ayush Nivesh Saarthi Portal 
serves as a dedicated gateway for domestic and international investors in the Ayush sector, 
providing comprehensive information to promote investment opportunities. The e -Charak 
portal functions as a virtual marketplace and information platform for the medicinal plants 
sector, connecting farmers, collectors, buyers, manufacturers, and exporters. 
The Y -Break Pro mobile application promotes holistic well -being in workplaces through 
short Yoga sessions. The mYoga application encourages regular Yoga practice by providing 
learning modules and guided sessions that can be accessed anytime and anywhere.  The Yoga 
Portal serves as a dedicated digital platform for promoting Yoga as a holistic lifestyle practice 
and enhancing its accessibility to all. It provides authentic and structured information on 
Yoga protocols, training modules, certified institutions, events, and research studies, ensuring 
credibility and ease of access for learners and practitioners. 
Further, Yoga Sangam , hosted on the Yoga Portal during the  International Day of Yoga 
(IDY) 2026 , witnessed the registration of over  7.6 lakh organizations  across the country . 
Among these,  441 organizations  were registered from the  Nabarangpur Parliamentary 
Constituency of Odisha , indicating active participation  from the constituency in the 
nationwide Yoga celebration. 
Collectively, all e -governance tools developed under the Ayush Grid are accessible to 
everyone and have strengthened service de livery, improved operational efficiency, and 
enhanced transparency and accountability. 
(b) The Ayush Grid has improved access to Ayush -based primary healthcare, including in 
rural and aspirational districts, by strengthening digital infrastructure and standardizing 
service delivery.  
Through platforms such as the Ayush Hospital Management Information System (A -HMIS), 
patient registration, electronic health records, referrals and continuity of care are being 
enabled digitally. As on 31st July 2026, a total of 6,245 Ayush health facilities across the 
country have been onboarded onto AHMIS . Regional Research Institute in Unani Medicine , 
Regional Research Institute in Homoeopathy and Central Ayurveda Research Institute have 
on-boarded on AHMIS application in Odisha. Real-time dashboards and standardized 
reporting further support monitoring, planning and targeted interve

INTEGRATING MODERN HEALTHCARE AYUSH SYSTEMS IN TAMIL NADU 
 
3327. SHRI C N ANNADURAI 
 
Will the Minister of AYUSH be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is promoting Tamil Nadu as a major destination under the ‘Heal 
in India’ initiative by integrating modern healthcare with AYUSH systems, including Siddha, 
Ayurveda and Yoga and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the details of the Central assistance provided for upgrading hospitals, wellness centres, 
Siddha institutions and medical tourism infrastructure in Tamil Nadu under the initiative; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to establish or strengthen dedicated centres offering 
Panchakarma, Siddha therapies, Yoga-based wellness and other holistic treatment facilities to 
attract domestic and international medical tourists in Tamil Nadu; and 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to promote Tamil Nadu's traditional systems of 
medicine globally, enhance quality accreditation, develop skilled manpower and generate 
employment through medical value travel and wellness tourism under the ‘Heal in India’ 
initiative? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (IC) OF THE MINISTRY OF AYUSH 
 
(SHRI PRATAPRAO JADHAV) 
(a) The Government has taken multiple initiatives towards integrating modern healthcare 
with Ayush systems across the country including Tamil Nadu which are as follows: 
i. The Ayush Vertical under Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), 
established by the Ministry of Ayush and Ministry of Health and Family Welfare 
(MoH&FW), serves as a dedicated institutional mechanism for planning, monitoring, 
and supervising Ayush -specific public health programs. This vertical provides 
technical support to both the Ministries in developing strategies for public health, 
healthcare, Ayush education, and training. 
ii. Government of India has adopted a strategy of Co -location of Ayush facilities at 
Primary Health Centres (PHCs), Community Health Centres (CHCs) and District 
Hospitals (DHs), thus enabling the choice to the patients for different systems of 
medicines under a single window. The engagement of Ayush doctors/ paramedics and 
their training is supported by the MoH&FW under National Health Mission (NHM), 
while the support for Ayush infrastructure, equipment/ furniture and medicines are

responsibilities.

‘Ayush Module -Internship e lectives’ for MBBS  students in Ayurveda, Unani and 
Siddha system of medicine. As per regulation 10 (7) of National Commission for 
Indian System of Medicine (Minimum Standards of Undergraduate Ayurveda 
Education) Regulations -2022, the proportion of modern advances in Syllabus for 
Ayurveda teaching content shall be up to 40 per cent. Homoeopathic Education Board 
under National Commission for Homeopathy (NCH) has taken various new initiatives 
like early clinical exposure, introduction of elective s, faculty development program, 
foundation program, finishing program at end of internship, inclusion of new subje cts 
like pharmacology and psychology to sensitize the students about different systems of 
medicine.

Ayush dispensaries and Ayush Health and Wellness Centres , now renamed as Ayushman 
Arogya Mandirs (Ayush) comes under the purview of State Government. However, Ministry 
of Ayush  is implementing the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of NAM through State/UT 
Governments a nd supporting their efforts in overall development of Ayush system. The 
State/UT G overnments may avail financial assistance by submitting suitable proposals 
through their State Annual Action Plans as per the provisions of NAM guideline . Under this 
scheme, the Government of India extended financial assistance to the State of  Tamil Nadu of 
Rs. 308.91 crore from 2014 -15 to 2025 -26 for various activities including upgrading 
hospitals, wellness centres, Siddha institutions and medical tourism infrastructure.

fully funded through grants -in-aid provided by the Ministry of Ayush for medical education, 
research, and healthcare services. The institute has an attached Ayothidoss Pandithar Hospital 
with inpatient bed strength of 220 and provides regular OPD services.

its peripheral Institutes / Units in Tamil Nadu. This organiza

Rajasthan on predefined cost sharing basis between the Central and the Sta te Governments to 
deliver various services for children in difficult circumstances. The scheme provides 
institutional care and non -institutional care. Child Care Institutions (CCIs) established under 
the Mission Vatsalya scheme provide, inter-alia, age-appropriate education, access to 
vocational training, recreation, health care, counselling etc. Under Non -Institutional Care 
Service, support is provided through Sponsorship, Foster Care, Adoption and After Care.  
  
The Ministry has launched the revamped Mission Vatsalya Portal which is an integrated 
Digital platform for all the stakeholders related to child protection services. Mission Vatsalya 
portal is a technologically upgraded secure portal which provides digital working platform for 
various stakeholders across different levels at State and district. The earlier Khoya -Paya 
portal, TrackChild services and CARINGS portal for adoption has been brought under this 
unified portal. 
  
The Mission Vatsalya scheme also provides for emergency outreach services (24x7x365) for 
children in difficult circumstances through Child Helpline (1098) which is integrated with 
Emergency Response Support System-112 (ERSS-112) Helpline of Ministry of Home Affairs 

and Women Helpline (181). Dedicated WCD -Control Room at State level for Child Helpline 
have been set up in all the 36 States and UTs.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3337 
ANSWERED ON 07.08.2026 
 
PROTECTION OF INDIAN SAILORS 
 
3337. SHRI THIRU THANGA TAMILSELVAN: 
 
Will the Minister of PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS be pleased to state: 
पȅन, पोत पįरवहन और जलमागŊ मंũी 
 
(a) whether it is true that India is the third largest supplier of sailors to the world after 
Philippines and China, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether it is true that last year alone around 1125 Indian sailors are reported to 
have been abandoned and many Indian sailors had been suffering from hunger and 
starvation for many months, if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) whether the Union Government has taken any steps to save Indian sailors from 
abandonment, hunger and starvation in the middle of the ocean and to protect their 
life and jobs, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS 
(SHRI SARBANANDA SONOWAL) 
 
(a)  As per the BIMCO/ICS Seafarer Workforce Report 2026, India is ranked as the 
second largest seafarer-supplying nation globally, with an estimated supply of over 
3.11 lakh seafarers (officers and ratings). 
(b)  As per the ILO/IMO Joint Database on Abandonment of Seafarers 1,373 Indian 
seafarers on 172 vessels were reported to be affected in abandonment cases during 
the year 2025. As on 04.08.2026, issues of 119 vessels with 1010 seafarers have been 
resolved. In abandonment cases, shipowners are responsible under the Maritime 
Labour Convention (MLC), 2006 to provide food, water, wages, medical care and 
repatriation. In cases where seafarers face  hardship, the Directorate General of 
Maritime Administration (DGMA) closely coordinates with Indian Missions abroad, 
RPSL agencies, shipowners, P&I Clubs and welfare organizations such as the 
International Transport Workers' Federation (ITF) to ensure provision of essential 
supplies and facilitate repatriation of affected seafarers. 
(c)  The Government has taken several measures to prevent seafarer 
abandonment and protect the welfare of Indian seafarers. These include strengthening 
the regulatory framework through amendments in the Merchant Shipping Act and 
issuance of regulatory notices/orders, mandatory verification of vessels prior to 

deployment, restriction and blacklisting of non-compliant vessels, enhanced 
monitoring of Recruitment and Placement Service Licence (RPSL) agencies, regular 
coordination with Indian Missions abroad for repatriation of stranded seafarers, 
awareness programmes for seafarers, and strict enforcement action against defaulting 
RPSLs. Further, welfare support mechanisms have been strengthened through 
financial assistance schemes for stranded seafarers and their families, besides 
continuous engagement with international organisations such as IMO, ILO and ITF for 
timely resolution of abandonment cases.

(a) to (c) As on date, 93 Passport Seva Kendras (PSKs) and 456 Post Office

Kendras (PSKs) and Post Office Passport Seva Kendras (POPSKs) across the

3
which a passport can be applied for at any PSK/POPSK. The Passport Mobile  
Vans have been widely deployed to allow on-site passport processing in  
remote, rural, hilly and less serviced areas.
  At  PSKs,  the  applications  for  passports  and  related  services  are 
processed  on  the  same  day,  subject  to  document  submission  and  
verification,  and  are  forwarded  to  the  concerned  authorities  for  further

queries. These digital initiatives have substantially reduced the need for  
physical  visits  for  administrative  inquiries  while  improving  accessibility, 
convenience and service delivery.

4

to  fill  vacancies  through  the  Staff  Selection  Commission  and  through 
deputation from other services. It has also engaged young professionals,  
data entry operators and multi-tasking staff on contract basis in various  
RPOs.
(e) To address the issues regarding citizen grievances, delays, and com -
plaints, the Ministry has set up Public Grievances Cells and monitors all  
communications received through emails and social media closely. RPOs  
have been sensitised to promptly attend to all passport related grievances  
in a timely manner. Passport adalats are conducted to clear pending pass -
port applications. Self-service kiosks/feedback screens have been installed

(a) Ministry of Ayush  has taken following steps to promote the production, quality, 
standardisation and export of A yush medicines:  
1. The Drugs & Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Drugs Rules, 1945 have exclusive regulatory 
provisions for Ayush drugs.  It is mandatory for the manufacturers to adhere to the prescribed 
requirements for licensing of manufacturing units & medicines including proof of safety & 
effectiveness, compliance with the Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) as per Schedule T 
and Schedule M-I of the Drugs Rules, 1945 for Ayurved a, Siddha, Sowa -Rigpa, Unani and 
Homeopathy drugs respectively and to follow the quality standards of drugs as prescribed in 
the respective pharmacopoeia. 
Drug Inspectors collect medicine samples regularly from manufacturing firms or retail 
shops within their jurisdiction and send them to Drug Testing Laboratory under Drug Control 

department for quality testing and if any sample is found to be ‘Not of Standard Quality’, 
appropriate action is initiated to prevent the sale of such medicines in the market, along with 
legal proceedings as per the provisions of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and the Rules 
made thereunder. There are 34 Drug Testing Laboratories available in State/UTs for testing of 
the Legal Samples drawn by the Drug Inspectors of concerned State/UTs. 
2. The Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H), a 
subordinate organization under Ministry of Ayush, develops pharmacopoeial standards and 
formulary specifications for Ayush drugs, which serve as the official compendia for 
determining their identity, purity, and strength. Compliance with these standards is mandatory 
under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and the Rules made thereunder. PCIM&H also 
functions as the Appellate Drug Testing Laboratory for Ayush drugs and conducts regu lar 
capacity-building programmes for Drug Regulatory Authorities, Drug Analysts, and other 
stakeholders on standardization, quality control, and testing methodologies to strengthen the 
quality assurance system for Ayush drugs. 
3. Drug Testing Laboratories are approved by Ministry of Ayush under Rules 160A to 160J of 
the Drugs Rules, 1945, for carrying out tests relating to the identity, purity, quality and strength 
of Ayush drugs. As on date, 118 private Drug Testing Laboratories have been approved by 
Ministry across States and Union Territories for conducting such tests in accordance with the 
provisions of the Drugs Rules, 1945. 
4. Further, Ministry of Ayush is implementing a Central Sector Scheme, namely, Ayush 
Oushadhi Gunvatta Evam Uttpadan Samvardhan Yojana (AOGUSY) to support Ayush 
Pharmacies and Drug Testing Laboratories to achieve higher standards like World Health 
Organization Good Manufacturing Practices ( WHO-GMP) and National Accreditation Board 
for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL) respectively. 
5. In addition, Ministry of Ayush has undertaken the following initiatives to promote quality 
assurance and export of Ayush products: 
• World Health Organization Certificate of Pharmaceutical Product (WHO-CoPP) is issued 
by Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) after joint inspection of 
manufacturing units by drug inspectors posted in Ayush Vertical in CDSCO along with 
drug inspectors of States/UTs and CDSCO for compliance with WHO Technical Report 
Series (TRS) guidelines for herbal medicines.  
• Ministry of Ayush has launched Ayush Quality Mark (AQM) initiative through the Ayush 
Export Promotion Council (AYUSHEXCIL). Under this framework, the Ayush Quality 

Mark is being granted after scrutiny and verification of valid quality certifications and 
statutory approvals issued by the competent Government authorities, such as WHO-GMP, 
Ayush Premium Mark and other recognised certifications, as applicable. 
• Ayush Standard Mark and Ayush Premium Mark are awarded to Ayush Drugs by Quality 
Council of India (QCI) based on third -party assessment of compliance with prescribed 
National and International quality standards.

 Will the Minister of Chemicals and Fertilizers be pleased to state:

during the last three years, year-wise and State-wise; 
 
(b) whether the Government has received any complaints from farmers 
regarding the shortage of DAP/pesticides; 
 
(c) if so, the number of such complaints received during the last two years, along 
with the details of the areas worst affected due to the said shortage; 
 
(d) the reasons for the said shortage such as import constraints, decline in 
domestic production, distribution related issues, etc.; and 
 
(e) the steps taken by the Government to resolve the shortage and ensure the 
timely availability of fertilizers and pesticides to farmers? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS 
 
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
 
(a) to (e) Following steps are taken by the Government every season for ensuring 
timely and adequate availability of fertilizers in the country: 
 
(i) Before the commencement of each cropping season, Department of Agriculture 
and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with all the State Governments, 
assesses the State-wise & month-wise requirement of fertilizers. On the basis of 
requirement projected by DA&FW, Department of Fertilizers (DoF) allocates 
adequate quantities of fertilizers to States by issuing monthly supply plan and 
continuously monitors the availability. 
 
(ii) The movement of all major subsidized fertilizers is monitored throughout the 
country by an on-line web-based monitoring system called integrated Fertilizer 
Management System (iFMS). 
 

(iii) The gap between demand (requirement) and production for Urea & other 
fertilizers is met through imports. The import for the season is also finalized well 
in advance to ensure timely availability.  
 
(iv) The State Governments are regularly advised to coordinate with manufacturers 
and importers for streamlining the supplies through timely placement of indents. 
 
(v) Regular coordination is done with the Ministry of Railways for giving sufficient 
rakes, priority to fertilizers and for timely evacuation of rakes for States. 
 
(vi) The distribution of fertilizers within the State at district/block level is done by the 
concerned State government. 
 
In view of above, the availability of fertilizers viz. Urea, DAP, MOP and NPKS has 
remained adequate in the country during the ongoing Kharif 2026 season. The State-
wise information regarding availability position of these fertilizers in last 3 years and 
during the ongoing Kharif 2026 season (as on 03.08.2026) is placed at Annexure. 
 
Further, as informed by DA&FW, Registration Committee constituted under section 5 of 
the Insecticides Act, 1968 grants registration certificates for generic pesticides 
expeditiously to ensure the availability of pesticides at reasonable prices. Further, as per 
the assessment carried out by DA&FW in consultation with major pesticide associations, 
it is indicated that sufficient inventory of pesticides is available in the country for the 
ongoing Kharif 2026 season. As per the data available for FY 2025-26, the pesticide 
production reported by the DCPC stands at  3,02,974 MT in comparison to 2,87,267 MT 
during 2024-25.

entries.t: Ex Parte Civil and Family Court Cases
entries.head:
1 
 
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LAW AND JUSTICE 
DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3344 
TO BE ANSWERED ON FRIDAY, THE 07th AUGUST, 2026 
 
EX PARTE CIVIL AND FAMILY COURT CASES 
 
3344. DR. AMAR SINGH: 
 
Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be pleased to state:  
(a) whether the Government is aware that ex parte orders are being passed in civil and family court 
cases where one of the parties is unable to appear or effectively defend their case due to mental illness, 
intellectual disability, serious medical condition or other circumstances beyond their control; 
(b) whether any guidelines or safeguards exist to enable courts to ascertain the capacity of such absent 
parties before proceeding ex parte, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government has collected data on such cases, if so, the details thereof and if not, the 
reasons therefor; and 
(d) whether the Government proposes to amend the law or issue directions to ensure appointment of 
a guardian, legal aid counsel or other appropriate representation for vulnerable persons before ex 
parte orders are passed, so as to uphold the principles of natural justice? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF LAW  
AND JUSTICE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF  
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
 
(SHRI ARJUN RAM MEGHWAL) 
 
(a) to (c): Ex parte proceedings in civil and family court cases are governed by the provisions of the 
Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (CPC) , the Family Courts Act, 1984 , and other applicable laws. 
Under the CPC, a court may proceed ex parte only after being satisfied that summons has been duly 
served and the party has failed to appear in accordance with the prescribed procedure. 

2 
 
Adequate statutory safeguards already exist under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (CPC), 
which provides remedies for setting aside an ex parte decree  (Order IX, Rule 13 ) where sufficient 
cause for non-appearance is established. Further, where a party is of unsound mind or is otherwise 
incapable of protecting his or her interests on account of mental infirmity, the CPC contains 
provisions for representation through a next friend or guardian  (Order XXXII Rule 15 , read with 
Rules 3 and 4), as the case may be.  
The courts exercise their judicial discretion in accordance with the facts of each case and the 
applicable law. No separate guidelines have been issued by the Central Government in this regard. 
No centralized data is maintained by the Government regarding ex parte orders passed in civil 
or family court cases specifically involving persons suffering from mental illness, intellectual 
disability, serious medical conditions, or other similar circumstances beyond their control. 
(d): Legal services institutions constituted under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 provide 
free legal services to eligible persons in accordance with the provisions of the Act  and uphold the 
principles of natural justice. At present, there is no proposal under consideration of the Government 
to amend the law or issue separate directions in this regard.

colleges in Bihar at a total approved cost of Rs. 1,628 crore. Further, under the CSS for
Strengthening and Upgradation of State Government Medical Colleges for starting new PG

disciplines and increasing PG seats, 314 PG seats have been approved in 07 Government
Medical Colleges in Bihar at a total approved cost of Rs. 212.42 crore.
Government has approved Phase-III of the Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) for
strengthening and upgradation of existing State Government/ Central Government Medical
Colleges/ Standalone PG Institutes/ Government Hospitals for increasing 5,000 PG seats and
extension of the CSS for upgradation of existing government medical colleges for increasing
5,023 MBBS seats with an enhanced cost ceiling of Rs. 1.50 crore per seat from financial
year 2025-26 to 2028-29. Guidelines for implementation of these schemes have been issued
in November 2025, wherein, States and UTs including Bihar have been requested to send the
Detailed Project Report with proper Gap Analysis. However, as of now, no proposal has been
received from the state of Bihar.

Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:

 LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3349 
ANSWERED ON 07.08.2026  
  
IMPLEMENTATION OF ONE STOP CENTRES  
  
3349. SHRI DARSHAN SINGH CHOUDHARY:  
  
(a)  whether the Ministry has reviewed the implementation of One Stop Centres (OSCs), 
Women Helplines and other support services being operated under Mission Shakti; if 
so, the details thereof including the number of women benefitted from these services 
in the Hoshangabad–Narsinghpur Parliamentary Constituency during the last few 
years; 
  
(b)  whether the Ministry has reviewed the effectiveness of the measures for the prevention 
of crimes against women and children and the coordination mechanism among various 
Departments; if so, the details thereof;  
  
(c)  whether the Government is aware of any cases in which women have again been 
subjected to domestic violence/harassment even after a settlement through OSCs; if so, 
the details thereof; and 
  
(d)  whether any special provisions/policy are in place for stringent legal action against 
such habitual offenders, special monitoring, protection of the victim and prevention of 
recurrence; if so, the details thereof?  
  
 
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR)  
   
(a) to (d):   The Government gives utmost priority to the safety, security, rehabilitation and 
empowerment of women in the country. Government has adopted multi -pronged approach to 
address the needs of women on a life -cycle continuum basis for their educational, socia l, 
economic and political empowerment so that they become equal partners in fast paced and 
sustainable national development. This vision of 'Women led development' is essential for 
realising the goal of a developed India, or 'Viksit Bharat' by 2047.  
Mission Shakti aims at strengthening interventions for women safety, security and 
empowerment. Mission Shakti comprises of two verticals 'sambal' for safety and security of 
women and 'Samarthya' for empowerment of women across the country.   

One Stop Centre (OSC) is a component of the Sambal vertical under the umbrella Mission 
Shakti. It provides integrated and immediate support and assistance under one roof to women 
affected by violence and those in distress, both in private and public spaces  all across the 
country. It provides services like medical aid, legal aid and advice, temporary shelter, police 
assistance and psycho-social counselling to needy women across the country. Since inception, 
i.e. 1st April, 2015 to 30th June, 2026, 991 One St op Centres have been made operational 
across the country and over 15.20 lakh women have been assisted in the country through these 
OSCs. As on date, 63 One Stop Centres are operational in the State of Madhya Pradesh 
including one OSC each in the districts of Narmadapuram, Narsinghpur, Raisen of the 
Hoshangabad–Narsinghpur Parliamentary Constituency and over 1.65 lakh women in the 
State  have been assisted since inception.  
Women Helpline (181) is also a component of the Sambal vertical under the umbrella Mission 
Shakti. Women Helpline (181) provides 24 -hour toll -free telecommunication services to 
support women in both emergency and non -emergency situations. Since inception t ill 30th 
June, 2026, over 1.04 crore women have been assisted in the country and out of which 3.83 
lakhs women assisted are from Madhya Pradesh.   
To strengthen convergence and ensure seamless access to support services, OSCs have been 
integrated with the Women Helpline (WHL), and so far, 661 OSCs have been integrated. 
Through this integration, women can be referred to appropriate services in a timel y and 
coordinated manner. Further, the Women Helpline has been integrated with the Emergency 
Response Support System (ERSS -112), Child Helpline (1098) and other relevant service 
delivery mechanisms to facilitate prompt emergency response and effective inte r-agency 
coordination. In addition, OSCs have also been integrated with Shakti Sadan to enable referral 
of women requiring long -term institutional support, rehabilitation and safe accommodation, 
thereby ensuring a continuum of care under the Mission Shakti  framework. 
Mission Shakti is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme and implementation of this scheme lies with 
the State Governments and UT Administrations. Adequate staff and infrastructure support is 
provided for smooth operationalization of Mission Shakti Scheme across the  country. 
Further, once in a year, the Programme Approval Board (PAB) monitors with States and UTs 
the progress of activities under the scheme and reviews status of achievement of objectives, 
effective delivery of services to women and children.  Apart from this, officials of the Ministry 
continuously review the scheme through meetings, video conferencing and by making field 
visits to States/UTs from time to time. The Ministry has also developed the Mission Shakti 
Dashboard,

entries.t: Regulation and Patient Safety in Dental Implantology
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
DEPARTMENTOF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3350
TO BE ANSWERED ON 07TH AUGUST, 2026
REGULATIONAND PATIENTSAFETY IN DENTALIMPLANTOLOGY
3350. SHRI PARSHOTTAMBHAIRUPALA:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government is aware of the absence of a comprehensive national regulatory
framework governing dental implants, implant biomaterials, artificial teeth and implantology
practices, resulting in potential patient-safety risks, if so, the details thereof;
(b) whether the Government proposes to mandate scientific evaluation of implant devices,
including fatigue, biocompatibility, sterility and corrosion testing and establish a National
Dental Implant Registry with mandatory device traceability and adverse-event reporting, on
the lines of international best practices, if so, the details thereof; and
(c) whether the Government proposes to prescribe mandatory practitioner certification,
accreditation of implant centres, standardized informed-consent protocols and ethical
advertising norms for dental implant procedures, if so, the details thereof?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SMT. ANUPRIYAPATEL)
(a) & (b): All Medical Devices including dental implants, implant bio materials, artificial
teeth etc., are regulated under the provisions of Drugs and Cosmetics Act 1940 and Medical
Devices Rules 2017, regarding quality, safety & performance of the Medical Devices in the
country.
Under the said rules, requirements of scientific evaluation of medical devices
including implantable medical devices are prescribed and the manufacturer has to perform all
the tests applicable as per existing standards for biocompatibility, sterility along with other
tests as applicable for its compliance before grant of license. The scope of standards, essential
principles for safety & performance and Quality Management System (QMS) are mandatory
for ensuring the safety & quality of the medical device throughout the device life cycle.
Further, the existing rules are aligned with global regulatory practices followed by stringent
regulatory authorities.

As regard to adverse-event reporting mechanism, the Indian Pharmacopoeia
Commission (IPC), functions as the National Coordination Centre (NCC) for the
Materiovigilance Programme of India (MvPI). The programme collects and analyses
suspected adverse event associated with medical devices, including devices used in dentistry
to ensure medical device safety.
Further, as part of Quality Management System (QMS) implementation, the
manufacturer has to adhere to the requirements of Quality Risk Management for vigilance
reporting and all Adverse Events (AE) are monitored by the manufacturer as per their Quality
Risk Management protocol. The manufacturer also needs to submit Post Market Surveillance
(PMS) report mentioning all Adverse Events to the Licensing Authority, for ensuring Quality,
safety & performance of the Medical Device throughout the product life cycle.
(c): As prescribed at present, any registered Dentist may perform dental implant
procedures.

MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3351  
TO BE ANSWERED ON 07.08.2026  
GENDER BUDGETING CELLS  
3351. MS. S JOTHIMANI: 
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
(a)  The details of the Ministries/Departments and State/UT Governments that have 
established Gender Budgeting Cells (GBCs) as mandated;  
(b)  Whether the Ministry has set clear timelines/milestones for setting up of GBCs in all 
remaining Ministries/Departments and States/UTs, if so, the details thereof;  
(c)  Whether the Government has formulated any strategy for systematic collection of 
gender- disaggregated/intersectional data to strengthen gender -responsive 
policymaking; 
(d)  whether the Government proposes to conduct an independent audit of the performance 
of existing GBCs, including how effectively they have influenced budget decisions and 
outcomes for women; and 
(e)  if so, the details of the mechanisms being adopted for data collection, coordination with 
the Ministries/integration of such data into programme design and budget decisions  
  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR)  
(a) to (e) The Charter of Gender Budget Cells was issued by the Department of Expenditure, 
Ministry of Finance. It lays down guidelines for constitution, composition and functioning of 
Gender Budget Cells (GBC) in all Ministries/Departments. Gender Budget Cells in 
Ministries/Departments are set up with the objective of influencing and effecting a change in 
the policies, programmes in a way that could tackle gender imbalances, promote gender 
equality and development; and ensure that public resources through Ministry’s budget are 
allocated and managed accordingly.  
Gender Budget Cell is envisaged to function as focal unit for coordinating Gender Budgeting 
initiatives in a Ministry/Department. The Charter indicates that GBC may discharge functions 
such as, Identification of programme with a view to analyse gender issu es addressed by them; 

Organizing discussions/consultations with all stakeholders for exchanging ideas and getting 
feedback on the efficacy of sectoral policies and programmes; Conduct performance audit for 
reviewing the actual physical/ financial targets of the programme etc. As per available 
information, Gender Budget Cells have been set up in 62 Central Ministries/D epartments and 
35 State/UTs. 
Ministry of Women and Child Development provides capacity building and technical support 
to central Ministries/ Departments/ States/ UTs to advance their gender budgeting processes. 
Financial support is also provided by the Ministry to training institutes to conduct training 
programmes for the government officials on Gender Budgeting. Ministries/ Departments/ UTs 
utilize their resources for ensuring proper implementation of the Gender Budget provisions 
either by themselves or through Implementing Agencies. They also monitor the progress, from 
time to time, for achieving the objectives of their schemes/ programmes. These 
Ministries/Departments report data in Output -Outcome Monitoring Framework (OOMF), 
which is an outcome monitoring framework for schemes of Go vernment of India, and also 
comprise gender related indicators in a few schemes of Ministries/Departments. Progress in 
gender related indicators is also assessed in national level sample surveys such as National 
Family Health Survey (NFHS), Periodic Labour  Force Survey (PLFS) etc. 
Every year Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance issues Budget Circular, 
which mandates all Ministries/Departments to report allocations for women and girls in the 
Gender Budget Statement in a prescribed format. The gender budget allocations,  which are 
compiled as Statement 13 of the Expenditure Profile of Union Budget, are prepared by 
Ministries/Departments/UTs for their schemes/programmes. An allocation of Rs. 5.01 lakh 
crore has been reported for welfare of women and girls in the Gender Bud get Statement of 
Union Budget for FY 2026 –27. This is an increase of 11.55% over the GBS allocation of Rs. 
4.49 lakh crore in FY 2025 –26. In FY 2026 -27, a total of 53 central government 
Ministries/Departments and 5 UTs have reported allocations as against 49 
Ministries/Departments and 5 UTs in FY 2025 –26.

MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
DEPARTMENTOF HEALTH RESEARCH
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3352
TO BE ANSWERED ON 7TH AUGUST, 2026
PREVALENCE OF STAPHYLOCOCCI BACTERIA
3352. DR. SAMBIT PATRA:
Will the Minister of HEALTHAND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government has conducted any study to assess the spread and prevalence of
Staphylococci bacteria in the country, if so, the details thereof;
(b) whether the Government proposes to formulate any policy to ensure comprehensive monitoring
and reporting of environmental Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR), if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the details of the action plan undertaken or proposed to be undertaken by the Government to
contain the spread of environmental antimicrobial resistance in the country?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a): Staphylococcus is a commonly found bacteria living harmlessly on skin of healthy human
beings. Most of the time Staphylococcus does not cause any harm, but it can sometimes cause
infections. It can also cause severe and even fatal infections particularly in healthcare settings, in
high-risk patients like those on invasive devices or with weakened immune systems.
Many Staphylococcus bacterial infections can be treated and cured with traditional antibiotics.
Some strains of Staphylococcus are antibiotic-resistant and need to be treated with newer antibiotics.
The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has informed that it has conducted hospital-based
surveillance through its Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance and Research Network (AMRSN)
across 20 tertiary care hospitals in the country. AMRSN collects and analyses Staphylococcus
aureus isolates obtained from clinical specimens and publishes annual reports on antimicrobial
resistance trends. Key findings are:
 In 2024, Staphylococcus species accounted for 13.2% of all bacterial isolates obtained from
clinical specimens under the surveillance network.
 The proportion of Staphylococcus isolates has declined from 18.7% in 2017 to 13.2% in
2024. Similarly, the proportion of Staphylococcus aureus isolates decreased from 12.5% in
2017 to 8.65% in 2024.
 Based on four years of surveillance across the participating hospitals, Staphylococcus aureus
(1.1%) infection was identified in 2,533 of 228,126 admitted patients. Of these, 1,190

infections were reported among ICU patients, corresponding to 1.6% (1,190 of 73,671) of
all ICU admissions.
(b) and (c): National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) has informed that under the National
Programme on AMR containment, it has established sentinel surveillance network for surveillance
of AMR in 9 priority pathogens causing clinical infections, one of them being Staphylococcus
aureus, the species responsible for most staphylococcal infections.
The Government has released the National Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance (NAP-AMR)
2.0 (2025-2029) for the containment of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). The Plan adopts One
Health approach and includes environmental AMR surveillance as one of its strategic priorities to
strengthen the monitoring and reporting of antimicrobial resistance across human, animal, food, and
environmental sectors.

entries.t: Budget Allocation for ABDM and U-WIN Platform
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
DEPARTMENTOF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3355
TO BE ANSWERED ON 07.08.2026
BUDGET ALLOCATION FOR ABDM AND U-WIN PLATFORM
†3355. SHRI LALJI VERMA:
SHRI NEERAJ MAURYA:
Will the Minister of HEALTH and FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the details of the total budget allocated under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission
(ABDM) and the U-WIN platform during the financial year 2025-26 in the country,
along with the actual expenditure incurred on the digital infrastructure of rural health
centres, State-wise and district-wise in Uttar Pradesh;
(b) the percentage of Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) card creation and
vaccination tracking cases pending in rural areas of the country due to power outages
and poor internet connectivity, State-wise including Uttar Pradesh;
(c) whether the Government has taken any concrete steps to identify pregnant women and
children who were deprived of registration due to complex portal procedures or server
downtime and to provide them alternative health benefits, if so, the details thereof;
and
(d) the details of the special schemes implemented by the Government to integrate poor
and backward sections living in remote rural areas, who lack smartphones and digital
literacy into the digital health ecosystem?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) to (d): Under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) financial assistance is
provided to States and Union Territories for supporting human resources deployed for ABDM
implementation, capacity building of various stakeholders and IEC (information, education &
communication) activities. The State/UT wise details of budget allocated and expenditure
incurred under ABDM for FY 2025-26 are at Annexure.
Inclusion is one of the key principles of ABDM. The Government has taken various steps to
ensure that the benefits of the mission reach every citizen. ABDM has provisions for assisted
mode in places where internet connectivity might be poor. Offline mode for creation of
ABHA has been added which enables delivery of services in regions of poor internet
connectivity, or on account of unavailability of hardware or both. The Government reference
PHR (Personal Health Record) application such as Aarogya Setu is multilingual and intuitive
to use, with a view to address the lack of digital literacy.
The U-WIN infrastructure has been developed with in kind support of international
collaboration. Key features of UWIN include ‘anytime access’ and ‘anywhere’ vaccination

services, generation of Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) and Child ABHA, self-
registration module, automated SMS alerts, QR based e-Vaccination Certificate and offline
mode for data entry by vaccinators. The offline functionality enables beneficiary registration
and recording of vaccination events in areas with poor internet connectivity. This feature
ensures uninterrupted service delivery during internet disruptions or power outages.

INITIATIVES FOR PROMOTION OF AYUSH  
 
3358. SHRI M MALLESH BABU  
Will the Minister of AYUSH be pleased to state: - 
(a) the details of the new initiatives launched by the Government to promote the production, 
quality, research, marketing and global acceptance of Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani, Yoga, 
Naturopathy, Sowa-Rigpa and Homoeopathy (ASU&H) medicines in the country; 
(b) the details of financial assistance, incentives and promotional schemes provided to 
manufacturers, start-ups and MSMEs engaged in the AYUSH medicine sector during the last three 
years, scheme-wise and State-wise, including Karnataka; 
(c) the steps taken by the Government to strengthen quality control, standardisation, 
pharmacovigilance and export promotion of AYUSH medicines; and 
(d) the measures taken by the Government to increase the availability of, public awareness of, 
certified AYUSH medicines through hospitals, Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, Jan Aushadhi outlets 
and digital platforms across the country? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (IC) OF THE MINISTRY OF AYUSH 
 
(SHRI PRATAPRAO JADHA V) 
(a) The Ministry of Ayush has launched several initiatives to promote the production, quality, 
research, marketing and Global acceptance of Ayush medicines. The major initiatives include: 
1. Ayush Oushadhi Gunvatta Evam Uttpadan Samvardhan Yojana (AOGUSY): Supports 
quality assurance, standardization, Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), testing 
infrastructure, pharmacopoeial standards and capacity building of the Ayush drug sector.  
2. AYURGYAN Scheme: Promotes evidence-based research, innovation, clinical studies and 
higher education in Ayush systems.  

3. Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H):  
Development and publication of pharmacopoeial standards, formularies and quality 
standards for Ayush drugs.  
4. International Cooperation  Scheme (IC Scheme) : Supports Indian Ayush drug 
Manufacturers/ Ayush Service providers to boost the export of Ayush products and 
services; facilitates the International promotion, development and recognition of Ayush 
systems of medicine; foster interaction of stakeholders and market d evelopment of Ayush 
at international level; promote academics and research through the establishment of Ayush 
Academic Chairs in foreign countries and holding training workshop/symposiums for 
promoting and strengthening awareness and interest about Ayush systems of Medicine at 
International level. 
5. Ayush Export Promotion Council (Ayushexcil): Facilitates export of Ayush products and 
services by supporting exporters through International exhibitions, seminars, buyer-seller 
meets, and capacity building of manufacturers and service providers.  
 
(b) Ministry of Ayush is implementing a Central Sector Scheme, namely, Ayush Oushadhi 
Gunvatta Evam Uttpadan Samvardhan Yojana (AOGUSY) to support Ayush Pharmacies and Drug 
Testing Laboratories to achieve higher standards like WHO Good Manufacturing Practices 
(WHO-GMP) and National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL) 
respectively. The components of scheme are as follows: - 
 
i. Strengthening and up -gradation of Ayush Pharmacies and Drug Testing Laboratories to 
achieve higher standards. 
ii. Pharmacovigilance of ASU&H drugs including surveillance of misleading advertisements. 
iii. Strengthening of Central and State regulatory frameworks including Technical Human 
Resource & Capacity Building programs for Ayush drugs. 
iv. Support for development of standards and accreditation/certification of Ayush products & 
materials in collaboration with Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Quality Control of India 
(QCI) and other relevant scientific institutions and industrial R&D centers.  
The details of financial assistance provided to Ayush Pharmacies and Drug Testing Laboratories 
including MSMEs during the last three years , State-wise including Karnataka is furnished at

pharmacovigilance and export of Ayush medicines- 
1. The Drugs & Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Drugs Rules, 1945 have exclusive regulatory

rigpa, Unani and Homeopathy drugs  respectively and to follow the quality standards of

NATIONALCENTRE FOR VECTOR BORNE DISEASES CONTROL
†3361: SHRI RAJU BISTA
Will the Minister of HEALTHAND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the total financial and technical assistance provided to West Bengal under the
National Centre for Vector Borne Diseases Control (NCVBDC) during the last five
years, year-wise;
(b) whether the Government has recorded rise in cases of vector-borne illnesses like
dengue, malaria, Japanese Encephalitis and scrub typhus in the rural and tea-garden
belts of North Bengal districts, if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the steps taken by the Government to evaluate and strengthen surveillance and vector
control infrastructure in this regard?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SMT. ANUPRIYAPATEL)
(a) to (c): Public Health is a State Subject and the responsibility for strengthening of
healthcare system lies with respective State/Union Territory Governments. However, under
National Health Mission (NHM), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of
India provides financial and technical support to the States/UTs including West Bengal in an
integrated manner for control of vector diseases, based on the Programme Implementation
Plans (PIPs) submitted by the States/UTs within their overall resource envelope.
Financial assistance provided during the last five years, year-wise is as below:
Financial Year 2021-22 2022-23 2023-24 2024-25 2025-26
Rs in Crores 12.96 13.6 14.28 35.98 31.25
The National Center for Vector Borne Diseases Control (NCVBDC) under the Ministry of
Health and Family Welfare administers an umbrella programme, namely, National Vector
Borne Diseases Control Programme (NVBDCP) for prevention and control of vector borne
diseases.
Total number of cases of Dengue, Malaria, Japanese Encephalitis and Scrub typhus reported
from North Bengal districts during year 2023,2024 & 2025 is at Annexure.
The following measures have been undertaken to prevent and control spread of vector borne

diseases and to evaluate and strengthen surveillance and vector control infrastructure in the
Country including in the rural and tea-garden belts of North Bengal districts:
 Provided Technical Guidelines for case management, prevention and control to the
States for implementation.
 Disease Management involving early case detection with active, passive and
sentinel surveillance followed by complete and effective treatment, strengthening
of referral services, epidemic preparedness and rapid response.
 Integrated Vector Management including Indoor Residual Spraying with
insecticide in selected high-risk areas, Long Lasting Insecticidal Nets in high
malaria endemic areas, use of larvivorous fish, anti-larval measures, source
reduction and fogging for combating outbreaks.
 Inter-Sectoral Convergence including high-level advocacy with allied ministries,
Human Resource Development through capacity building and policy development.
 Behaviour Change Communication and dissemination of public health messages
through various media platforms including social media, radio, newspapers and
electronic media.
 States are trained to enter the data on Integrated Health Information Platform-
Vector Borne Diseases (IHIP-VBD) portal for real time monitoring,
 Regular monitoring of disease situation is done through reviews and reports
submitted by the States/UTs.
 For surveillance and free diagnosis of Dengue and JE, a network of Sentinel
Surveillance Hospitals (SSHs) and Apex Referral laboratories (ARLs) are
identified across the country. NCVBDC provides IgM test kits free of cost to all
identified laboratories.
 The Government is actively collaborating with State Health Departments and
Urban Local Bodies to enhance sanitation, strengthen mosquito control measures,
and increase public awareness for the prevention and control of malaria and other
vector-borne diseases.
 To tackle malaria outbreaks and prevent further spread, the Government has
ensured adequate stocks of diagnostic kits and anti-malarial drugs at all health
centers and hospitals across the country.

(a) whether the Government has assessed the shortage of doctors, specialists, nursing officers
and paramedical personnel in Central Government-supported healthcare institutions,
including Government Medical College and Mahatma Gandhi Memorial (MGM) Hospital,
Warangal;
(b) if so, the details of the sanctioned strength, persons in position and vacancies,
categorywise;
(c) the steps taken by the Government during the last three years to fill such vacancies,
including recruitment, contractual appointments and other measures; and
(d) whether any proposal has been received from the Government of Telangana seeking
additional Central assistance for strengthening human resources in such institutions and if so,
the details thereof?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND
FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) to (d): ‘Public Health and Hospital’ is a state subject. The primary responsibility of
strengthening public healthcare system, including strengthening human resources lies with
the respective State/UT Governments. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare provides
technical and financial support to the States/UTs, including Telangana, to strengthen the
public healthcare system in rural areas based on the proposals received in the form of
Programme Implementation Plans (PIPs) under National Health Mission. Government of
India provides approval for the proposal in the form of Record of Proceedings (RoPs) as per
norms & available resources. Details of the approvals given for upgarading healthcare
facilities in Telangana are available at website of Ministry of Health and Family Welfare at
the Uniform Resources Locator (URL) as under:

https://nhm.gov.in/index4.php?lang=1&level=0&linkid=60&lid=73
The details of doctors, specialists, nursing officers and paramedical personnel in
Central Government and sanctioned strength, persons in position and vacancies can be
accessed at the following link of HDI 2023-24:
https://www.mohfw-dohfw.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/05/57202cf30629539e4d0fb0a2f700ac
62.pdf
Under NHM, following types of incentives and honorarium are provided for
encouraging doctors, specialists and nursing staff to practice in rural and remote areas of the
country to address the shortage of staff:
• Hard area allowances to specialist doctors for serving in rural and remote areas and
for their residential quarters so that they find it attractive to serve in public health facilities in
such areas.
• Honorarium to Gynecologists/ Emergency Obstetric Care (EmOC) trained,
Pediatricians & Anesthetist/ Life Saving Anaesthesia Skills (LSAS) trained doctors is also
provided to increase availability of specialists for conducting Cesarean Sections in rural &
remote area.
• Incentives like special incentives for doctors, incentive for Auxiliary Nurse and
Midwife (ANM) for ensuring timely Antenatal Checkup (ANC) checkup and recording,
incentives for conducting Adolescent Reproductive and Sexual Health activities.
• States are also allowed to offer negotiable salary to attract specialist including
flexibility in strategies such as “You Quote We Pay”.
• Non-Monetary incentives such as preferential admission in post graduate courses for
staff serving in difficult areas and improving accommodation arrangement in rural areas have
also been introduced under NHM.
• Multi-skilling of doctors is supported under NHM to overcome the shortage of
specialists. Skill upgradation of existing HR is another major strategy under NRHM for
achieving improvement in health outcomes.

3365. ADV. CHANDRA SHEKHAR
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state:-
(a) the key diplomatic roadmap and outreach campaign launched for  
India's  campaign  for  a  non-permanent  seat  on  the  United  Nations 
Security Council (UNSC) for the 2028–2029 term;
(b) the steps taken to build a global consensus on structural reforms of 
UNSC and text-based negotiations amidst increasing global polarization 
and institutional paralysis within multilateral bodies;
(c) the manner in which India plans to utilize expanded plurilateral  
forums, including expanded BRICS, Quad and I2U2, to advance the  
priorities of the Global South; and

2
(d) the financial and technical contributions committed by India towards 
international capacity-building programmes, including the training of  
more than 1.95 lakh individuals under capacity-building and scholarship 
initiatives?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH)
(a to d) India’s approach to its ninth term for a non-permanent seat on  
the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) 2028-2029 is based on  
SHANTI  –  Securing  Holistic  Advancement  through  Norms  Trust 
Integrity. The six priorities for the 2028-2029 candidature are: (i) A Voice 
of Global South (ii) Advancing Reformed Multilateralism (iii) A Future  
Ready Peacekeeping (iv) Addressing Threats Posed Due to Misuse of AI 
(v) Securing Maritime Commons, and (vi) Countering Terror Financing.
Government  of  India  accords  highest  priority  to  securing  
permanent  membership  for  India  in  an  expanded  UNSC.  This  is 
consistently taken up by India both bilaterally and multilaterally at  
various levels, including at the highest levels. India has also been  

3
advocating for early commencement of  text-based negotiations with  
clearly laid out timelines and milestones.

plurilateral formats have been used as the voice of peace, security and 
prosperity for all. Understandings reached through these initiatives  
have enabled India to strengthen relations with partner countries and  
put forward India’s viewpoint and shape the agenda on global issues  
such as reformed multilateralism, peace and security, climate change,  
transnational crime, fight against terrorism, cyber-security, energy and 
food security.
The Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) is India’s  
flagship international capacity building programme, implemented by  
Ministry  of  External  Affairs  as  a  bilateral development  partnership 
programme. Each year, approximately 12,000 slots are offered under the 
programme. It is estimated that more than 2.25 lakh individuals have
